items.title: π₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
items.title_zh: π₀：用流匹配连接语义与连续动作
items.summary: 在预训练视觉语言模型上构建流匹配动作架构，学习多平台、多任务机器人控制。

analysis.problem: 如何结合互联网级语义知识与复杂、高精度的连续机器人动作？
analysis.method: 以预训练 VLM 为基础，使用流匹配生成连续动作，并用多本体数据训练。
analysis.evidence: 摘要描述零样本、语言指令与微调设置；具体能力边界仍需核查正文。
analysis.limitations: 展示视频不能证明可靠性，需核对重复试验与失败分布。
analysis.question: 固定数据、模型规模与推理预算时，流匹配动作头的收益来自哪里？

items.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
items.title_zh: OpenVLA：开放的视觉语言动作模型
items.summary: 在预训练视觉语言模型上学习动作，研究开放 VLA 的跨任务能力与高效微调。

analysis.problem: 如何得到可访问、可微调并可迁移到新任务的视觉语言动作模型？
analysis.method: 融合预训练视觉特征与语言模型，通过机器人示范学习动作，研究低秩适配与量化。
analysis.evidence: 摘要给出多任务、跨本体与微调评测；比较前需核对任务、数据与控制设置。
analysis.limitations: 模型规模、预训练数据和动作表示的影响需要区分。
analysis.question: 固定任务数据预算时，预训练 VLA 与从头训练策略分别在哪些场景占优？

items.title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
items.title_zh: DROID：真实环境中的分布式数据采集
items.summary: 在多样化真实场景中分布式采集操作示范，支持研究数据多样性与策略泛化。

analysis.problem: 如何突破少数实验室环境限制，获得更丰富的真实操作示范？
analysis.method: 以分布式流程扩大场景、任务与采集人员覆盖。
analysis.evidence: 摘要报告 76k 条示范、564 个场景与 84 项任务；这些描述不能等同于泛化结论。
analysis.limitations: 数据规模与多样性的影响应通过受控实验区分。
analysis.question: 固定轨迹数量时，场景与任务多样性各贡献多少泛化收益？

items.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
items.title_zh: Open X-Embodiment：跨机器人数据与策略
items.summary: 联合多个机器人平台的数据与策略学习，为跨本体训练提供公开研究基础。

analysis.problem: 不同机器人收集的数据能否共同支持更通用的策略学习？
analysis.method: 聚合多本体数据，研究跨机器人策略训练与迁移。
analysis.evidence: 已核查论文元数据与项目入口，规模和迁移结果有待全文核查。
analysis.limitations: 动作空间、控制频率和采集分布的差异需要单独分析。
analysis.question: 统一数据格式后，哪些本体差异仍限制正迁移？

items.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
items.title_zh: ACT：低成本硬件上的精细双臂操作
items.summary: 通过低成本遥操作收集示范，用 Action Chunking with Transformers 建模动作序列，学习精细双臂操作。

analysis.problem: 低成本、精度有限的硬件能否从少量示范学习精细双臂任务？
analysis.method: ACT 预测动作块，通过动作序列建模缓解逐步预测的误差累积。
analysis.evidence: 摘要报告六个真实操作任务；不同任务成功率和示范条件需逐项核查。
analysis.limitations: 固定任务的结果不能直接说明新环境、新物体或跨本体泛化。
analysis.question: 动作块长度与反馈频率的最优组合是否随接触复杂度变化？

items.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
items.title_zh: Diffusion Policy：用扩散模型生成机器人动作
items.summary: 把视觉运动策略表示为条件去噪扩散过程，结合动作序列预测与滚动执行，处理多模态动作分布。

analysis.problem: 如何表达多种有效动作，并稳定生成连续的视觉运动动作序列？
analysis.method: 以视觉观测为条件，通过迭代去噪预测动作块，再按滚动时域执行。
analysis.evidence: 摘要报告四类操作基准上的十二项任务；基线、试验次数和统计差异仍需全文核查。
analysis.limitations: 迭代采样时延、多峰行为覆盖与分布外表现需分别评估。
analysis.question: 在相同数据与执行频率下，减少去噪步骤如何影响精细操作？

items.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
items.summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

items.title: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
items.summary: Robot foundation models have shown remarkable performance in robot control, yet adapting them to a new task still relies heavily on teleoperated demonstrations. Egocentric human videos offer a scalable substitute, but overlaying rendered robots on human videos or retargeting human poses into robot actions leaves significant visual or action gaps for high-DoF robot embodiments. To address this limitation, we propose RoboTryOn, which treats human-to-robot translation as virtual try-on: try-on keeps the person and swaps the garment, RoboTryOn keeps the demonstrated motion and swaps the human for the robot. Specifically, RoboTryOn converts a human video into a video of the target robot specified by a reference image, while preserving the original task, objects, and background. To maintain visual consistency, we translate selected keyframes autoregressively and use them to guide video synthesis with motion conditioned on the human hand skeleton. Additionally, we use an inverse dynamics model (IDM) that incorporates depth features to infer action labels from synthesized videos for policy learning. Our experiments across multiple humanoid embodiments show that policies trained with our synthetic data improve the average success rate on novel tasks, including challenging bimanual manipulation, from 2% to 60%, without any real robot demonstration of those tasks. Moreover, training with our synthetic data matches the performance of policies trained solely on teleoperated demonstrations at approximately a third of the collection cost, demonstrating the cost efficiency of our approach.

items.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
items.summary: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.

items.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.

items.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
items.summary: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Its high-level policy performs flexible sequence modeling of human and humanoid motion through a shared tokenized representation, generating reactive humanoid motion and anticipating the partner's motion when they are occluded, while a low-level whole-body tracking controller executes the generated motion on the robot. To train the system, we introduce a two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure that retargets one interaction partner to the robot while morphing the other partner to preserve contact dynamics, reachability, and relative body scale. We apply this procedure across five motion-capture datasets to produce a new Human-Humanoid Interaction (HHI) benchmark of 260 hours of human-humanoid interactions. Our results demonstrate that Social Humanoid produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world. Project page: https://von31.github.io/social-humanoid/

items.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
items.summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.

items.title: Radio-to-Pose Information for Gauge-Drift Correction in Cooperative Localization
items.summary: Cooperative localization uses odometry and inter-robot measurements to estimate the motion of a robot team. These measurements describe only relative geometry, but the team's estimated position and orientation can drift together over time, i.e., gauge drift. In this work, we study correction of this gauge drift using a radio attenuation map registered in the same world coordinate frame used for robot poses. Specifically, we propose Radio-to-Pose Information (RPI), an interface that converts power residuals and their pose derivatives into a Gaussian information matrix and vector pair. RPI builds on the insight that received power is sensitive to shared displacement in the world map. The pose estimator uses the interface together with odometry and inter-robot measurements to update poses and minimize uncertainty. We characterize the shared motions detectable from the map and observed links. For an uncertain shared map, RPI keeps correlations across robots and time and reproduces joint Gaussian pose estimates and covariances. Across $1000$ simulated Gaussian trials, RPI matches the results of joint estimation. Across 32 paired trials with a registered map, RPI reduces common-position RMSE from $0.542$m to $0.140$m in a $50\times50$m arena compared with a baseline that uses radio only to weight relative measurements.

items.title: GPWM: Modeling the World as 3D Particle Motion
items.summary: We introduce GPWM, a Generative Particle World Model that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time. Unlike video world models that generate scene appearance, GPWM operates directly in 3D physical space. A single representation and architecture cover rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials, in both passive physics and robotic interaction. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer that combines flow matching with diffusion forcing to generate coherent physical trajectories far beyond its training horizon. We train and evaluate GPWM on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus spanning diverse geometries, materials, interactions, and robot embodiments. GPWM outperforms the best prior learned-dynamics baseline in each of six physical domains, reducing prediction error by 31% on average. Breaking from the domain-specific setting of prior methods, a single Unified GPWM models these heterogeneous regimes with one set of weights, largely outperforming per-domain baselines and even surpassing our own specialist models in two domains. GPWM further generalizes to unseen geometries, physical properties, object counts, and rollout horizons. Beyond prediction, GPWM enables contact-rich planning by learning a generative prior over joint actuator-object motion. Instead of searching over unconstrained actions, planning searches the model's latent noise for interactions that achieve a desired object-space goal. With the same world model, noise-space planning substantially outperforms action-space search on pushing and picking, where complex contact sequences are hard to discover. Executed open-loop in simulation, the resulting plans achieve goal-directed manipulation without reference action trajectories or goal-specific policies.

items.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
items.summary: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.

items.title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model
items.summary: World-action models (WAMs) jointly model future traffic states and driving actions for end-to-end autonomous driving in intelligent transportation systems. However, their action learning remains dominated by expert-trajectory imitation, leaving unsafe alternatives close to expert trajectories insufficiently constrained. To improve WAM robustness in safety-critical scenarios, we propose NegWAM, a safety post-training framework for unified WAMs that learns explicit safety boundaries from near-expert failure trajectories. NegWAM constructs negative trajectories that are geometrically close to the expert trajectory yet carry safety risks, uses them as repulsive anchors to steer predictions away from dangerous behavior, and encodes them as scene-conditioned rider tokens to learn scene--trajectory compatibility. During training, NegWAM jointly optimizes the flow-matching and near-expert negative objectives, while the auxiliary rider branch is discarded at inference, incurring no additional overhead. On NAVSIM v2, NegWAM achieves 40.4 EPDMS on navhard, a 4.1% relative improvement over the strongest compared scorer-free WAM baseline, and achieves 93.3 EPDMS on navtest. These results demonstrate that NegWAM achieves strong performance in safety-critical scenarios while preserving routine-driving performance. Zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM further demonstrates cross-benchmark generalization. The code is available at https://github.com/Zizizi-hao/NegWAM.

items.title: FREE-LIVO: Physically Decoupled Yet Tightly Coupled LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry
items.summary: LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (LIVO) integrates complementary LiDAR, camera, and IMU measurements to achieve robust state estimation. However, most existing methods assume a fixed relative pose and accurate time synchronization between sensors. Toward modular and heterogeneous robotic systems, this paper presents FREE-LIVO, a tightly coupled odometry method that requires neither a rigid LiDAR-camera rig nor LiDAR-camera time synchronization. The proposed method uses a pretrained image feature matcher to establish correspondences between a camera image and a dense LiDAR intensity image generated from a single LiDAR scan using a generative model. From the resulting 3D point-to-pixel correspondences, we construct reprojection factors that directly constrain LiDAR and camera poses at different acquisition times. These factors are jointly optimized in a single factor graph together with constraints from point cloud registration, visual feature tracking, and the IMU measurements associated with each sensor. On six sequences from the public M3DGR dataset, FREE-LIVO achieves an average absolute trajectory error (ATE) RMSE of 0.45 m without provided LiDAR-camera extrinsic parameters and exhibits minimal accuracy degradation under time synchronization errors of up to 0.5 s. Furthermore, experiments with the LiDAR and camera mounted on separate robots demonstrate that the method can jointly estimate the trajectories of independently moving sensors.

items.title: Rethinking Self-Repair in Code-as-Policy Agents: What Drives Retry Success?
items.summary: Code-as-policy agents often use execution feedback to retry failed programs. Additional sampling and task guidance can also improve success, leaving the contribution of failure-specific feedback unclear. We study this question in simulated robot manipulation. A fixed lookup selects feedback templates using failure labels and the API variant. A frozen code model generates a fresh program after each scene reset. On the same 252 initial failures, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B recovers 85.3% within five retries, compared with 68.3% for resampling with the same retry cap. The advantage persists under fixed total-token budgets. Feedback from other episodes and fixed task guidance yield similar recovery point estimates, with no detected benefit from matching the coarse failure label. In a separate study, a fixed guided prompt used from the first attempt achieves an observed overall success rate similar to that of template-based feedback. Template-based feedback also lowers recovery on a nut-insertion task requiring a rim grasp, consistent with an incompatible center-grasp instruction. Evaluations of robot self-repair should include resampling, mismatched feedback, and concise, task-compatible static guidance as baselines.

items.title: RAFT: Reasoning-Aligned Fine-Tuning Improves Robustness of VLA Post-Training
items.summary: Adapting a generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a target task with limited demonstrations can improve nominal task success while reducing robustness to variations in appearance, objects, and instructions. We introduce reasoning-aligned fine-tuning (RAFT), a two-stage post-training procedure: RAFT first trains low-rank adapters on task-relevant reasoning annotations, then freezes them while fine-tuning the policy on action demonstrations. On a physical DROID robot, RAFT achieves $75.0\%$ out-of-distribution success, compared with $27.9\%$ for plain fine-tuning; on a multi-stage bimanual YAM task, it reaches $70.0\%$ mean success, compared with $36.0\%$ for the strongest baseline. RAFT also improves success under visual, object, and instruction shifts in simulated pick-and-place and open-drawer tasks. Compared with plain fine-tuning, RAFT policies place more attention on annotated task regions and yield higher linear-probe accuracy for object identity in later layers. A broader reasoning-data mixture further improves downstream success across demonstration budgets.

items.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
items.summary: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. We further identify and fix a silent rendering corruption whose rate rises sharply along compute-heavy planning paths while leaving the official direct-policy result unaffected, and release a detector, fix, and scripts. These findings show why test-time scaling should be audited as a chain of premises (decision signal, realized efficiency, evaluationintegrity) rather than by success rate alone. Conclusions are scoped to the tested configuration.

items.title: Concertina: Embodying Manipulation and Cognition in One Diffusion Vision-Language Model
items.summary: Most vision-language-action (VLA) policies decouple manipulation from cognition by bolting an external action mechanism onto a vision-language model (VLM)--either quantizing actions into discrete tokens whose errors bear no stable correspondence to physical displacements, or delegating continuous trajectory generation to a separate action expert whose gradients compete with or are blocked from updating the VLM backbone. We argue that manipulation and cognition should instead be embodied in the same model, shifting from a decoupled VLA to an Embodied Vision-Language Model (eVLM). We introduce Concertina, an eVLM that places continuous trajectory representation, blockwise generation, and physical-coordinate supervision directly on the computation and parameter path of a shared diffusion VLM backbone. Each control timestep is encoded as one continuous latent action token in the backbone hidden space, and the shared Transformer reconstructs temporally ordered action blocks via the same corrupt-and-reconstruct operator used for multimodal pretraining. Active action projections account for only 0.21% of parameters in the 4.46B model with zero separate action-generator layers, compared with 16.5%-35.1% dedicated action-expert capacity in representative continuous VLAs. Using our proposed Action Interface Audit, we confirm that cross-time trajectory coupling emerges in the middle and late layers of the shared backbone rather than at the action interfaces. On standard benchmarks, Concertina achieves 98.15% average success on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on the 10,030-task LIBERO-Plus benchmark, and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D. Code: https://github.com/lose4578/Concertina Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/Traly/concertina

items.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.

items.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.

items.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
items.summary: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.

items.title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents
items.summary: Latent communication enables agents to collaborate efficiently by directly exchanging intermediate model representations rather than raw sensor data or text messages. Existing approaches, however, are primarily designed for LLM agents and do not consider the bandwidth constraints and heterogeneous task deadlines faced by cyber-physical agents. In this work, we propose SCALE, a real-time latent communication method tailored for cyber-physical agents. Motivated by the spatio-temporal continuity of the physical world, SCALE matches tokens across consecutive latent messages using similarity scores to identify reusable information and avoid redundant transmission. It then profiles the semantic gain and communication cost of transmitting different amounts of latent information. Based on these profiles, SCALE employs a real-time scheduler that jointly determines which pending messages to transmit and how many latent tokens to send, subject to available bandwidth and task deadlines. We evaluate SCALE across three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study under diverse network conditions and heterogeneous task deadlines. Our results show that SCALE significantly improves both task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SCALE-4E80/.

items.title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
items.summary: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution feedback support effective code refinement, and how task specifications and previously acquired skills influence robustness and task transfer. We further investigate the efficiency and capability of the resulting programs when deployed without involving an online agent for decision-making. Across eight real-world tasks, PyRUA-REAL achieves an average success rate of 91.1%. In complementary evaluation on 42 tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, it achieves an average success rate of 84.4%. This study provides empirical guidance for turning physical exploration into reusable robot skills that support continued improvement and robust, efficient deployment.

items.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
items.summary: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal). Yet existing simulators idealize these sensors, hiding critical modality-specific failure modes that limit real-world deployment. We present VisionSIM, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities. We expose fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters, reproducing failure modes overlooked by general-purpose simulators: pileup and glare for LiDAR; phase wrapping, saturation, and motion artifacts for iToF; refractory drops for event cameras; and history-dependent emission for thermal cameras. This enables principled cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. We release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground-truth annotations.

items.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

items.title: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration
items.summary: Frontier-based exploration systems repeatedly evaluate geodesic travel costs between robot poses and candidate viewpoints, and tour-based planners consume the full pairwise distance matrix built from them. Recomputing these matrices with one graph search per source scales with the explored map size, whereas distance caches that refresh only locally affected or newly created frontiers can retain stale costs between surviving pairs when newly discovered free space creates a global shortcut. We present H-TRIP (Hierarchical Tropical Rank-one Incremental Propagation), an exact distance index grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring for monotonically growing occupancy grids. H-TRIP partitions the known map into a spatial hierarchy with fixed boundary ports. Each unknown-to-free revelation is decomposed into efficient rank-one min-plus edge insertions at the affected leaf, and only decreased port-to-port summaries are propagated along its ancestor chain. A shared hierarchical lift evaluates the dense many-to-many matrix of shortest distances for all active query points on the occupancy map. We prove that sequential insertions preserve exact shortest-path distances on the grid. Benchmark experiments confirm exact agreement with reference searches on fully built maps and show that dense many-to-many queries at a few dozen viewpoints are up to two orders of magnitude faster than sequential k x BFS. On exploration runs with sixteen robots, in-loop queries on the growing occupancy graph are 2.21x-8.59x faster than co-scheduled k x BFS on maps with side 256, 512, and 1024 cells.

items.title: VABAR: A Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics
items.summary: For robots to operate reliably in commercial and industrial applications, they must persistently perform specific tasks with known variations in object shape and pose. We call this Variational Automation (VA) to differentiate these settings from fixed automation. Inspired by recent papers on Agentic Robotics, where pretrained LLM and VLM coding agents combine interpretable robot programming with the open-world adaptability of model free policies, we propose a general set of agentic robotics benchmark design criteria that includes accessibility, repeatability, diversity, relevance to agentic robotics and practical applications, physical realizability, resistance to benchmark saturation, and computational efficiency. We instantiate these principles in six manipulation task classes spanning industrial, medical, and infrastructure applications: tool sorting, tool hanging, gear meshing, syringe packing, cable insertion, and cable routing. We introduce the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics (VABAR), an open, easily replicable, simulation-based manipulation benchmark to systematically evaluating agentic robotics systems. Built fully on open-source tools, VABAR features detailed implementations using the Newton physics engine, standardized task variations, difficulty tiers, success metrics, and a library of 33 generalizable skills with human-authored programmatic reference solutions. We provide initial baseline evaluations using an open agentic manipulation harness, Graph-as-Policy (GaP), and Isaac Lab Arena.

items.title: Where Is VLA Inference Time Spent? Bottlenecks and Optimization Interactions Across GPUs
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map camera observations and language instructions to robot actions. However, their large backbones and repeated action generation can make inference take longer than the robot's real-time requirements for its next action. To reduce the load of VLA computations, researchers have proposed multiple optimization approaches, including quantization and pruning. These optimizations can be combined with other general optimizations such as better kernel compilation or using CUDA graphs instead of the eager mode. However, most of these optimization results are usually reported on a single GPU type, typically for a few VLA models, with no analysis of what the real bottlenecks are for a model on a particular hardware or how these optimizations would generalize beyond the reported results. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive measurement study of seven families of inference optimization methods, from CUDA graphs and compilation to token pruning and quantization, on seven state-of-the-art VLAs evaluated on four GPU families ranging from a datacenter H100 to an embedded Jetson Thor. We analyse how CPU launch overhead, memory bandwidth, and kernel efficiency jointly shape optimization gains, and how applying one method changes the benefit of another. From this analysis, we derive VLA-Triage, guidelines for stacking optimizations under latency budgets. The guidelines identify which stages can provide the required savings and which combinations need testing in the deployed execution mode.

items.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
items.summary: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\% vs. 0.63\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. The results show faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set. Ablations suggest that simulated alternatives provide useful early supervision, while executed outcomes alone sustain later performance. We also demonstrate the method on a real robot to verify the simplicity of integrating the method to real bin packing pipelines.

items.title: Symmetry-Aware Surrogate-Assisted Testing of UAVs
items.summary: We investigate a symmetry-aware surrogate-assisted testing approach for UAV autopilots. The proposed approach exploits geometric symmetries between flight missions by trans- forming obstacle configurations into a shared canonical coordi- nate frame. This enables a neural-network surrogate trained on a single reference mission to be reused across arbitrary missions, reducing the amount of high-fidelity simulation data required for training. The surrogate model is trained to predict the minimum clearance distance between a UAV and surrounding obstacles and is used to guide test generation towards safety-critical scenarios. We evaluate this approach using the Aerialist UAV test bench and benchmark its performance against techniques from the 2024 to 2026 UAV Testing Competitions. Results show that the approach achieves an average critical-test-case hit rate of 42% across the evaluated missions, compared with approximately 10% for the constrained-random baseline used to generate the training data. This approach also achieves high input diversity and competitive benchmark performance. However, our findings reveal limitations in transferring surrogate predictions across missions with differing flight-path characteristics, highlighting the boundaries of geometric canonicalization. To support reproducibility and future research, we provide the trained surrogate model and a dataset comprising more than 2,500 high-fidelity simulations.

items.title: Energy-Aware Open-Vocabulary Detection Scheduling for Low-Power Robotic Autonomy
items.summary: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) lets robots search for run-time object queries, but fixed-rate inference spends embedded compute on low-value frames during idle motion, map revisits, or stable viewpoints. This paper presents an energy-aware OVD scheduler for low-power mobile robots. The scheduler uses odometry, map change, and detector confidence to switch among low-, mid-, and high-power YOLO-World-S modes on a Jetson Orin Nano. We evaluate the energy-quality trade-off on an AgileX LIMO using 40 real navigation trials: two target objects, five placements per target-policy pair, and four perception policies. Across bottle and cup trials, the scheduler records 8/10 mission success compared with 7/10 for each fixed-rate baseline, while reducing mean Jetson input power (a Jetson-side power-draw metric) by 5.2% relative to an 8 Hz high-rate baseline and lowering achieved OVD call rate by 34.0%. It does not minimize mission-window Jetson input energy because longer missions can erase instantaneous power savings. A separate 60 s stationary microbenchmark isolates the perception workload: the scheduler lowers mean power from 8.045 W to 7.301 W and energy from 484.7 J to 438.1 J relative to the 8 Hz baseline. These results support robot-state-aware OVD scheduling as a promising power-management mechanism with competitive task reliability, while showing that mission-window Jetson input energy must be read together with task progress and runtime.

items.title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. Each decision processes hundreds of visual tokens, often across multiple cameras, leading to substantial computation while allowing irrelevant background content to distract action prediction under distribution shift. We argue that these issues stem from two complementary forms of redundancy: many visual tokens are spatially irrelevant, while attention over the remaining tokens is often misallocated. Based on this observation, we propose T3R, a Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement framework. In the first stage, segmentation-guided token pruning removes irrelevant visual patches to reduce computation and eliminate distracting context. In the second stage, saliency-guided attention biasing reallocates attention toward action-critical visual regions and language instructions within the retained tokens. Together, pruning produces a cleaner candidate set, while attention biasing further emphasizes the most decision-relevant evidence, yielding a better accuracy-efficiency frontier than either stage alone. On LIBERO-Spatial, T3R removes 85% of scene-camera visual tokens while essentially matching the unpruned success rate, and improves success by up to 7 percentage points under out-of-distribution object-placement perturbations. The timing comparison attributes 7.8 ms per inference call to pruning and attention-bias application. As input resolution increases, LLM-forward profiling shows up to a 3.3x speedup over the unpruned baseline. Evaluations across LIBERO, SIMPLER, and RoboTwin with three VLA backbones show the strongest accuracy-efficiency benefits in multi-camera settings. These results demonstrate that training-free token refinement is a practical approach to efficient and robust VLA inference.

items.title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented. We present MOMASPLAT, a novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions. Our key insight is that standard MoMa data collection naturally provides the multiview observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D. MOMASPLAT combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to separately reconstruct the scene and manipulated object, render them from novel viewpoints, and generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations paired with transformed actions. We evaluate MOMASPLAT on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation. MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.

items.title: AffectiveVLA: Safe and Intent-Aware VLA Control for Human-Humanoid Social Interaction
items.summary: Social touch interactions, such as handshakes, fist bumps, and hugs, require humanoid robots to infer human intent, generate contact-rich motions, and maintain safe physical contact. We present AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pipeline deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. A lightweight RGB-based model recognizes interaction intent from two onboard cameras and converts it into a language prompt for the VLA policy. Low-confidence predictions suppress motion execution, reducing unintended activations. During physical contact, interaction-specific compliance profiles adjust arm impedance, while an independent voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe-stop procedure. Using VR teleoperation, we collected approximately 1,300 multimodal interaction episodes and fine-tuned four VLA models: GR00T, RLDX-1, Being-H0.5, and UnifoLM-VLA-0. On-robot evaluation identifies GR00T as the best-performing standalone model. Integrating intent recognition increases its macro-F1 score from 0.75 to 0.90, while the intent model achieves a p95 inference latency of 6.27 ms. These results demonstrate that explicit intent gating improves the reliability of VLA-based social interaction without compromising real-time operation.

items.title: Compounding Physical RSI: Turning Execution Failure into Inherited Capability
items.summary: Generalist robot policies are trained on static offline datasets, yet physical manipulation unfolds sequentially across stages. Because a weakness in a downstream stage remains unobservable until the policy passes earlier ones, each resolved bottleneck exposes the next hidden failure mode. This staged structure calls for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), in which a policy iteratively executes, diagnoses failures, and updates itself. Moreover, because task completion behaves like a product of stage-level pass rates, recursive gains can multiply across generations. In physical environments, three bottlenecks obstruct compounding: terminal execution feedback rarely localizes the stage that caused a failure, failed trajectories do not supply the corrective action, and updating shared parameters can degrade previously mastered skills. We propose Compounding Physical RSI, a self-evolving policy framework that turns execution failures into heritable capability. First, automated capability-gap assessment traces failed rollouts to the task stage where progression breaks down and formulates a structured improvement objective. Second, conditioned on this objective, our remedy stage curates validated, stage-relevant experience and refines the policy via behavior-regularized offline reinforcement learning, without requiring costly online rollouts at each optimization step. Third, to safeguard existing skills, our retention stage constructs weight-space candidates between the inherited reference policy and the refined policy, evaluates them across the task suite, and promotes the best candidate as the reference state for the next generation. Evaluated across all 42 tasks of the RoboDojo-Sim benchmark, CSU-AI-07 ranks first on the leaderboard with a three-seed mean Overall Score of 26.15 and Success Rate of 20.70%, outperforming the next-best entry by 5.92 points and 5.82 percentage points.

items.title: Detecting Silent Action-Interface Mismatch with Calibrated Relational World Models
items.summary: A robot action can satisfy shape and range constraints yet carry the wrong semantics: axes may be permuted, signs inverted, rotations rescaled, or gripper polarity reversed. We study learned state-action-effect relations as offline contracts for detecting these mismatches and ranking their likely fields. Clean held-out transitions calibrate alarms; a fixed inverse vocabulary supports closed-set localization. On ten LIBERO Spatial tasks comprising 432 source episodes, a capacity-controlled comparison at 2.5% empirical clean false-positive rate gives 46.1% recall for a ridge forward residual, 61.0% for a four-component joint Gaussian mixture, and 65.7% for the exact conditional of that same mixture. The joint score retains a 14.9 percentage-point advantage over ridge, while conditioning improves recall by a further 4.7 points. Joint scoring instead has higher localization: 95.8% versus 94.6%. These matched-rate comparisons are retrospective diagnostics, not deployment calibration guarantees. Earlier Object/Goal results broaden tasks within the LIBERO convention; DROID, all three HYDRA tasks, short temporal faults, small offsets, exact repair, and simulated mitigation fail their respective gates, while xArm contributes one task only. The evidence supports a bounded offline diagnostic and a detection-localization tradeoff, rather than joint-density superiority or cross-robot safety.

items.title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
items.summary: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. Yet existing approaches either cover only a limited set of skills, or forego motion priors entirely and produce unnatural behaviors, leaving the combination of a unified skill set and human-like motion quality unaddressed. We present soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that resolves both limitations through a structured latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture data. By constraining policy learning within this dynamically plausible motion manifold, a single skill-conditioned policy naturally learns to perform moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking in a unified formulation, while inherently producing human-like motion and fluid transitions during commanded skill switching. Augmented by robustness-oriented simulation design, soccerbot transfers zero-shot to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating agile, natural, and robust execution of the full soccer skill repertoire under real-world conditions.

technology_briefs.title: 视觉语言动作模型（VLA）
technology_briefs.tagline: 让机器人把“看到的场景”和“听到的指令”变成动作。
technology_briefs.why: 它把通用视觉语言知识接入机器人控制，是理解通用操作模型的一条核心主线。
technology_briefs.update: 异步 VLA 把低频语义推理与高频动作控制拆开，让大模型思考时，小型动作模型仍能持续响应。

mechanism.title: 看场景、听指令
mechanism.text: 相机图像与语言指令进入模型，形成与任务相关的表示。

mechanism.title: 生成动作
mechanism.text: 动作模块根据任务表示与当前观测预测机器人动作。

mechanism.title: 边做边更新
mechanism.text: 执行后继续观察。异步架构分别更新语义记忆与动作，训练时考虑记忆滞后。

technology_briefs.example: 以“把红杯放进盒子”为例：模型需要把杯子的颜色、盒子的位置与抓取动作联系起来。这个例子用于说明任务流程。
technology_briefs.boundary: 理解指令与可靠执行需要分别评测；异步系统还要处理旧语义记忆与新场景不一致的问题。
technology_briefs.question: 在相同数据和控制频率下，语义更新变慢到什么程度会影响动态任务？
technology_briefs.selection_reason: 按理解通用操作、预测、数据、控制和动作表示的学习价值组织；属于编辑导读顺序，不是性能排名。

technology_briefs.title: 世界动作模型（WAM）
technology_briefs.tagline: 预测动作会造成什么变化，用对未来的判断帮助机器人行动。
technology_briefs.why: 多步任务既要知道接下来做什么，也要处理眼前的接触和运动；预测模型把这两类信息带入动作生成。
technology_briefs.update: HiLo-WAM 用稀疏的长时视觉流描述任务演进，用密集的短时视觉流描述局部交互，再把两者与动作连接。

mechanism.title: 理解长时目标
mechanism.text: 较稀疏的视觉序列覆盖更长时间，提供任务历史与未来变化的线索。

mechanism.title: 预测局部变化
mechanism.text: 较密集的短时视觉序列描述机器人与物体的具体交互。

mechanism.title: 共同指导动作
mechanism.text: 两种时间尺度交换信息，并与机器人动作一起建模。

technology_briefs.example: 整理桌面时，长时信息描述清理进度，短时信息描述手靠近杯子后会发生什么。这个例子用于理解时间尺度。
technology_briefs.boundary: 看起来合理的预测仍可能误导控制。相关的 TIF 工作研究用真实执行反馈审计预测奖励，避免只凭高预测分选择训练轨迹。
technology_briefs.question: 固定推理预算时，更多算力应该分给更远的未来，还是更细的局部交互？
technology_briefs.selection_reason: 按理解通用操作、预测、数据、控制和动作表示的学习价值组织；属于编辑导读顺序，不是性能排名。

technology_briefs.title: 从人类视频学习机器人技能
technology_briefs.tagline: 把人的示范转成机器人能学习的数据，减少逐项遥操作采集。
technology_briefs.why: 适配新任务常受机器人示范成本限制。利用人类视频，研究的是如何把更易获得的经验转成可执行技能。
technology_briefs.update: RoboTryOn 保留任务、物体和背景，把示范者替换成目标机器人，再用包含深度特征的逆动力学模型推断动作标签。

mechanism.title: 取得人类示范
mechanism.text: 从人的任务视频中提取运动线索。

mechanism.title: 合成机器人视频
mechanism.text: 用目标机器人参考图和手部骨架等条件生成对应视频。

mechanism.title: 补动作、训练策略
mechanism.text: 逆动力学模型推断动作标签，再将合成数据用于策略学习。

technology_briefs.example: 看到人演示双手搬放物体后，系统尝试构造目标机器人执行该动作的训练材料。这是流程示意，不表示任意视频都能直接使用。
technology_briefs.boundary: 生成画面中的运动还需要满足真实机器人的动作约束；合成数据的收益应结合本体、任务和真实执行条件判断。
technology_briefs.question: 哪些任务最容易出现“视频看起来正确，但动作标签不可执行”的问题？
technology_briefs.selection_reason: 按理解通用操作、预测、数据、控制和动作表示的学习价值组织；属于编辑导读顺序，不是性能排名。

technology_briefs.title: 强化学习驱动的精密控制
technology_briefs.tagline: 通过交互与反馈，学会把机械臂移到目标并稳定保持。
technology_briefs.why: 高层模型给出目标后，底层仍需准确落地。稳定的反馈控制关系到精细操作与动作迁移。
technology_briefs.update: PolicyIK 用目标条件强化学习更新关节参考位置，同时观察参考与实际关节的偏差，并用到达、保持奖励训练精度。

mechanism.title: 测量目标误差
mechanism.text: 比较末端当前姿态与目标姿态，同时保留不同精度尺度的误差信息。

mechanism.title: 更新关节参考
mechanism.text: 策略根据反馈逐步调整关节位置参考，接近目标时缩小动作增益。

mechanism.title: 奖励到达与保持
mechanism.text: 训练既关注到达目标，也关注持续留在容差范围内。

technology_briefs.example: 把物体放到指定位置后还要稳住，不能只在某一帧碰巧达到目标。这个例子说明“到达”与“保持”的差别。
technology_briefs.boundary: 仿真与真机结果要分别看；控制器比较还需对齐时间预算、容差、机器人模型与任务分布。
technology_briefs.question: 接近目标时的精度收益，分别来自误差表示、动作增益还是保持奖励？
technology_briefs.selection_reason: 按理解通用操作、预测、数据、控制和动作表示的学习价值组织；属于编辑导读顺序，不是性能排名。

technology_briefs.title: 扩散与流匹配动作生成
technology_briefs.tagline: 像生成图像一样生成一段连续动作，表达同一任务的多种做法。
technology_briefs.why: 连续控制经常有多种合理动作。生成式策略提供了表示动作分布、预测一段动作序列的方法。
technology_briefs.update: Diffusion Policy 用条件去噪生成动作序列并滚动执行；π₀ 在视觉语言模型上构建流匹配动作架构。

mechanism.title: 以当前观测为条件
mechanism.text: 图像、任务等信息约束要生成的动作。

mechanism.title: 逐步生成动作序列
mechanism.text: 扩散策略通过迭代去噪生成动作；流匹配通过学习的流生成连续动作。

mechanism.title: 执行后重新预测
mechanism.text: 动作序列与反馈频率要一起设计。Diffusion Policy 使用滚动时域执行。

technology_briefs.example: 同一个杯子可以从不同方向抓取。策略需要保留多种有效做法，避免简单平均动作产生无效路线。这个例子解释多模态动作。
technology_briefs.boundary: 生成质量、推理时延和反馈频率共同影响部署。基础方法的发布时间已标明，不能把它们当成本周的新论文。
technology_briefs.question: 固定推理与数据预算时，生成步骤数、动作块长度和反馈频率怎样配合？
technology_briefs.selection_reason: 按理解通用操作、预测、数据、控制和动作表示的学习价值组织；属于编辑导读顺序，不是性能排名。

signals.title: La-JEPA：让策略容量摆脱生成骨干的约束
signals.paper_title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
signals.delta: 用V-JEPA 2.1表征代替生成VAE，随机初始化World/Action DiT；联合future/action流匹配，动作只读观察KV，推理删future并缓存观察，容量可独立于生成骨干选择。
signals.before: Fast-WAM/Faster-WAM虽已只在训练预测未来，仍部署大视频DiT及文本编码器；图像/语言生成骨干使控制器容量和部署成本难独立选择。
signals.after: S/B/L部署0.74/0.98/1.78B而非仅训练参数0.10/0.34/1.14B；纠正LIBERO-Plus指令后86.3/87.3/88.0%。优化S17.78ms对Fast88.09ms，但eager和图构建有不同取舍。
signals.relevance: 适合资源受限但已有目标示范的WAM方案选择：优先检查表示系统、训练时预测与容量分配，按完整policy call及部署库存评估；同时核数据/指令管线，不能照抄跨协议SOTA表。
signals.caveat: 作者实验未复现；感知/文本仍预训练，许多设计对照含数据、接口或训练步混杂。RoboTwin随机B仅35.4%、L缩放不单调；实机70/80对π0.5的69/80不确证广泛胜出。GPU型号未明确，仓库当前为空，未核实现。
signals.question: 相同参数和另行匹配训练算力时，将容量从Action转向World能否改善随机泛化，而不损clean成功与真实延迟？

evidence.label: 训练时预测的辨别性对照
evidence.context: 表7，原数据/评测管线三训练seed，future对action-only平均+2.12pp、配对p均<0.01；两目标各seed选到同IID checkpoint，不与88.0%新版主表作直接相减。

evidence.label: 纠正语言后重测
evidence.context: 表14，8493非语言变体恢复原训练指令，1537语言变体保留原扰动；NowWAM86.2不变。统一步限/episode权重，仅实际重测模型有纠正分，不是训练泄漏或无条件所有基线SOTA。

evidence.label: RoboTwin与容量边界
evidence.context: 表2/12，新版管线、clean示范训练、三seed各5000例/条件；均值B60.8%高于L59.0%，不能假定大模型总更强。JEPA-WAM全50任务图点是回归估计。

evidence.label: 完整调用与实现依赖
evidence.context: 表15，10去噪步32动作、单消费GPU优化版；含编码/准备/host输出，排除编译/模拟/机器人通信，型号未明确。eager S99.96ms慢于Faster62.70ms，原核图S34.20ms；不能说所有构建均5倍。

evidence.label: 实机范围
evidence.context: 表5/17，Franka四任务各20次、共400示范，dish以正确餐具位置及前序全成功计。LaPushT更好但dish16/20低于π18/20，且成功条件dish58.1s慢于39.0s；不证明全面同等或超越。

mechanism.title: 固定预训练表示与可选控制容量
mechanism.text: V-JEPA和冻结FLAN-T5提供先验，两个控制DiT随机初始化。无额外机器人预训练不代表无感知预训练；库存应含两编码器。

mechanism.title: 训练未来、推理不读未来
mechanism.text: future/action独立流噪声，注意力掩码阻断future进动作；监督塑造共享World参数。推理KV缓存后只迭代Action，非候选行动条件的在线世界模拟。

mechanism.title: 配方与评测一起核对
mechanism.text: tube-motion、dropout、增强/LoRA和冻结future预存构成配方，A–F块参考不同。指令修复、示范过滤、状态对齐和模拟版本改变均可影响分数，不把混杂收益归于单模块。

signals.change_type: 紧凑世界动作策略与评测纠正
signals.evidence_level: 全文文字已精读 · 引文匹配通过 · 未复现
signals.experiment_suggestion: 待验证假设：在目标数据有限时，相同策略参数预算下缩小Action DiT并将容量分配给World DiT，可比等宽同深的扩模方式保留clean成功并提高随机场景泛化。仅公开仿真实验草案：固定新版RoboTwin2438 clean示范、V-JEPA/文本编码器与LoRA、观察增强/目标、150k更新和评估器，比较等宽B、World较宽/Action较窄、反向分配三组，投影参数也计入同约0.37B预算；另设无future监督控制以区分正则化和容量效果。因World处理future tokens，等参数不等FLOPs，先测预计算+训练FLOPs/GPU小时，另做等总训练算力的对照，分别报告，不能冒称同时已严格匹配。至少3个独立训练seed，checkpoint只由独立clean验证集选择，各5000个clean/random终测episode，按任务及训练seed报告区间；随机集只终测不作架构选择。记录同GPU精确型号、部署权重、显存和10步完整查询eager/图/编译时延，核动作差异与闭环成功，而非只测DiT。预注册clean非劣界和random改进门槛，并看每任务失败与dish等精确动作需求。若等参数或等训练算力条件下随机优势消失、只靠更久训练/挑OOD checkpoint，或clean与实际延迟明显恶化，则推翻容量重分配改善取舍的假设。实验未执行、未创建选题，未全面查新；待实现可核验后再复现，不宣称研究空白。
signals.hypothesis_suggestion: 待验证假设：在目标数据有限时，相同策略参数预算下缩小Action DiT并将容量分配给World DiT，可比等宽同深的扩模方式保留clean成功并提高随机场景泛化。

changes.title: 未来只作训练监督，推理缓存观察KV
changes.text: 每层action queries读取World DiT观察KV及自身action，观察token仅看观察、future token看观察与future、action看观察与action，互不把future直接送入动作。训练分别给动作/未来采样独立噪声与流时间，两项MSE等权；未来损失通过共享World参数塑造观察表示。按图2掩码，未来分支并非读取候选动作的在线rollout，所以不能把其成绩解读为行动条件仿真规划收益。推理删future token、固定World时间0，观察KV每层只算一次，Euler迭代只跑Action DiT；预测32动作，LIBERO执行10、RoboTwin24后重规划。

changes.title: 双帧观察与跨未来片段目标，正则化和特征预存构成实际配方
changes.text: 每相机独立编码，tube观察为当前及前一帧；tube-motion未来由每隔两帧的16帧联合编码成8个时间网格，覆盖32帧。它是训练目标的双向编码，非策略偷看未来。观察和未来用归一化与空间缩减，LIBERO均池化，RoboTwin拼接patch；各相机至少保留一路，文本/本体条件也dropout。最终观察增强并LoRA适配编码器，future仍来自未增强帧的冻结编码器预存特征，减少反复编码16未来帧的成本。150k更新、LIBERO batch128/RoboTwin400。没有报告完整预计算+训练墙钟或GPU小时，较少可训练参数不能直接换算训练费用降幅。

changes.title: 0.10B可训练与0.74B部署是不同成本口径
changes.text: 表16：LIBERO S/B/L训练约0.10/0.34/1.14B，部署0.74/0.98/1.78B，含V-JEPA0.305B和FLAN-T5-large0.341B，LoRA合并、跨相机编码器只计一次。RoboTwin投影不同，分别0.11/0.37/1.17B训练、0.75/1.01/1.82B部署。L1.78B对NowWAM7.1B约四分之一，但S对JEPA-WAM1.35B并非四倍小。部署库存是权重规模，不是峰值显存或每动作FLOPs；部分基线无encoder-only数而计入未执行decoder，可能高估其实际执行规模。编码器选择与架构容量同时变化，不能把所有成本差归为同等视觉/语言先验下控制DiT的独立收益。

checks.title: 设计块各有参考，增强与token对照存在管线混杂
checks.text: 表6的A–F块只在块内比较，不是可相加收益清单。LIBERO相机dropout从仅腕到任一路也改了期望缺失流数0.10→0.19；增强/LoRA相对plain的+7.2点比较还改变在线编码和所选训练步。RoboTwin增强+LoRA的+16随机场景收益伴随2400→2500示范和评估实现变化；patch grouping相对均池化+4.1点也有full/95%数据、目标归一化与投影差异。表12最终新版管线将clean提高约5–8点、random降低约5–9点，平均变≤1点；不能混用旧44.7与新35.4作同一B模型的统一结论。保持目标冻结的对照未显著优于EMA目标（p=0.096），只能说未发现替换收益。

checks.title: 保留小规模设计和空仓库缺口，不把实现声明当已审计资源
checks.text: 多数设计单seed，优化未系统搜索LR、dropout、LoRA和World/Action相对容量，RoboTwin缩放非单调的成因未隔离；所有强结果限目标数据、这些模拟/四实机任务，尚无跨本体大规模机器人预训练检验。作者声明代码含预计算/训练/评估及S/B/L配置，但本轮访问github.com/mt-clemente/lajepa公开页明确显示仓库为空，未验证实现、权重或原始评估数据，不宣称已可复用代码。计时GPU具体型号、训练总GPU小时/显存等不足以独立复建成本。其主要贡献仍是紧凑控制DiT加预训练特征与有辨别力的设计研究，不应读成不需要预训练、无未来模型监督也同样好，或全面超过大基础策略。

attention.headline: La-JEPA：让策略容量摆脱生成骨干的约束
attention.summary: 在预训练视觉表征上训练小型策略，把未来预测留在训练阶段；推理只生成动作，让策略容量可以独立选择。

signals.abstract: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

signals.title: RoboTryOn：从人视频合成机器人演示与动作
signals.paper_title: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
signals.delta: 自回归生成机器人关键帧，以手骨架流插值全视频，再用跨本体IDM标手关节动作、以重建腕平移作IK校正；策略训练用合成演示，部署直接看原始相机图像。
signals.before: 固定机位人视频经直接手重定向加遮罩/渲染，视觉与可执行抓握仍有差距；新任务灵巧手遥操作人时昂贵。
signals.after: 两本体七OOD任务加入合成数据，平均归一化得分约2.1%→60.0%；只用合成数据训练策略约44.4%。新任务不用机器人演示，但生成器/IDM已有8.82小时跨本体机器人先验。
signals.relevance: 适合已拥有本体先验与固定标定相机、需要扩充桌面灵巧手任务的采集决策；可降低任务级人时，需同时预算离线合成算力与精细接触验证。
signals.caveat: 作者实验未复现；每任务28次，双臂每手完成各0.5，60%不是整项双臂任务完全成功率。基线为作者复现扩展，生成器有额外机器人先验；移动相机、力/紧插接不支持，RB-Y1 Air Fryer仍0%。GR-1仅视频展示。

checks.text: 人视频从机器人头相机位置拍，训练颈部与底座固定，IDM只预测固定颈/底座；移动视角的野外自我中心视频超出当前分布。依赖相机标定、双目与手重建精度，不能恢复力，也不能修复超出可达空间或手形能力的演示。图15有透明杯消失、手指穿把手、IDM闭手位置偏差；RB-Y1 Air Fryer0与未见细粒度插指抓握及长手指推走物体相联系。两本体桌面策略验证之外，GR-1仅生成视频，无该机策略执行证据。每任务28次且缺多seed统计，原始评分/训练材料本轮未审计；作者实验未复现，不能据生成样例推广任意本体、移动操作、紧配合插接或力控任务。

attention.headline: RoboTryOn：从人视频合成机器人演示与动作
attention.summary: 把人类示范视频中的人换成目标机器人，再推断动作标签，用于训练新任务策略；生成和动作标注模型的额外成本仍需核对。

signals.abstract: Robot foundation models have shown remarkable performance in robot control, yet adapting them to a new task still relies heavily on teleoperated demonstrations. Egocentric human videos offer a scalable substitute, but overlaying rendered robots on human videos or retargeting human poses into robot actions leaves significant visual or action gaps for high-DoF robot embodiments. To address this limitation, we propose RoboTryOn, which treats human-to-robot translation as virtual try-on: try-on keeps the person and swaps the garment, RoboTryOn keeps the demonstrated motion and swaps the human for the robot. Specifically, RoboTryOn converts a human video into a video of the target robot specified by a reference image, while preserving the original task, objects, and background. To maintain visual consistency, we translate selected keyframes autoregressively and use them to guide video synthesis with motion conditioned on the human hand skeleton. Additionally, we use an inverse dynamics model (IDM) that incorporates depth features to infer action labels from synthesized videos for policy learning. Our experiments across multiple humanoid embodiments show that policies trained with our synthetic data improve the average success rate on novel tasks, including challenging bimanual manipulation, from 2% to 60%, without any real robot demonstration of those tasks. Moreover, training with our synthetic data matches the performance of policies trained solely on teleoperated demonstrations at approximately a third of the collection cost, demonstrating the cost efficiency of our approach.

attention.headline: SuperMimic：用可微世界模型降低全身控制训练预算

signals.abstract: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.

signals.title: VLA-Tug：用失败前缀训练更早的监测信号
signals.paper_title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
signals.delta: 把失败轨迹的起点至失败时刻全部标正，丢弃失败后的损失；成功轨迹全标负。用骨干embedding上的LSTM读出分数与故障模式，再以LTT同时认证误报上限和早期检测下限，无合格阈值就拒绝认证。
signals.before: SAFE式trajectory标签将失败轨迹所有时刻标正，易混入已经失败的特征；单侧conformal只约束误报，不要求同时达到某个早期检出率。
signals.after: 将监督限制在失败前缀，以首次告警是否不晚于标注失败时刻评估；另外用带成功/失败标注的校准episode检验两项风险，并报告认证覆盖率。主要面积比较仍用MC，联合LTT单列评估。
signals.relevance: 做VLA失效监测时，先复现同探针的标签消融，再决定是否增加CLIP辅助头。部署决策应同时看可认证覆盖率、任务外漂移、动作块内观测盲区，以及能否给干预留出实际时间。
signals.caveat: 跨任务无形式保证；86%是部分目标下认证子集的FPR达标份额，不是双指标联合保证。真机检测只高0.7点且对时刻定义敏感，恢复仅有启发式案例。所有数值来自作者，未复现。
signals.question: 要求至少提前一个400ms动作块报警后，失败前缀监督还优于全轨迹标签吗？

evidence.label: 同模型、同头，仅换监督标签
evidence.context: 表9，pre-onset对trajectory，差17.4个百分点；分别±7.0/±3.9为拆分标准差。面积为FPR 0–0.4内早期TPR积分除以0.4，非任务成功率。

evidence.label: 联合证书有拒绝成本
evidence.context: 表7，认证子集seen两指标均达标；unseen FPR/早期TPR分别71%/57%达标，未给联合份额。α10%时0/14次可认证；不同校准方法分母须分开。

evidence.label: 辅助语义头不是稳定增益来源
evidence.value: 未见技能：去辅助头43.6，完整39.0
evidence.context: 表9，同pre-onset LSTM；分别±11.5/±7.0。作者未发现CLIP或模式头对检测的一致帮助；模式分类能力另行评价。

evidence.label: 真机小优势会随失败时刻翻转
evidence.context: 表6/11，VLA-Tug对SAFE-LSTM的早期面积，真机399条轨迹。原始只高0.7点；平移标签未重训，不能据此宣称稳定真机领先或量化恢复收益。

mechanism.title: 复用一次VLA调用的骨干表示
mechanism.text: 平均两相机与指令token后拼为6144维，单层256隐藏LSTM累计历史；三个小头输出告警分数、故障模式和辅助语义表示，在线不额外运行CLIP。

mechanism.title: 丢弃失败后的训练损失
mechanism.text: 最终失败episode在t≤t_fail全部标正，之后排除；成功episode全标0。它是在学习最终失败的前缀线索，并未指定固定的未来失败时间窗。

mechanism.title: 校准同时报告阈值与能否认证
mechanism.text: 对episode误报和早期漏检做LTT联合检验，从通过者选阈值；样本不足或目标过严时拒绝认证，分布外数据只作经验评测。

signals.change_type: 监测方法 · 监督与校准
signals.evidence_level: 全文文字已精读 · 引文匹配通过 · 未复现
signals.experiment_suggestion: 待验证假设：pre-onset相对全轨迹标签的优势，在要求至少一个动作块提前量后仍能保留。固定GR00T与LIBERO-X数据、骨干层、LSTM、训练预算和任务拆分，比较pre-onset、trajectory、仅前窗三种监督；另做有/无CLIP控制。用独立验证集选模型，以seen校准集固定FPR≤20%目标，记录LTT认证率及拒绝次数。测试集失败时刻由两名不了解方法的标注者分别判读并保留分歧区间，不用unseen结果选阈值。分别计算t_det≤t_fail−τ的召回，τ取0、0.4、0.8、1.2秒，报告固定FPR的早期召回、lead-time分位数、无告警率、模式准确率与episode级误报，同时作时刻正负1秒扰动。以任务为单位bootstrap差值，区分同一unseen任务重复seed与独立任务。若0秒优势在0.4秒或更大提前量下消失、超过标注不确定性后无法区分，或认证覆盖率降到无可用阈值，就推翻“检测提升足以支持整块动作前干预”的解释；若只某技能失效则缩小适用范围。实验尚未运行，未全面检索相关工作，不能称为已发现空白。
signals.hypothesis_suggestion: 待验证假设：pre-onset相对全轨迹标签的优势，在要求至少一个动作块提前量后仍能保留。

changes.title: 探针输入和参数：复用骨干，不额外运行CLIP
changes.text: π0.5取归一化后的第18层，GR00T-N1.7取第16层；分别平均agent相机、腕部相机和未padding指令token，拼接为6144维。单层256隐藏单元LSTM接三个64隐藏ReLU的MLP，输出标量分数、10类模式及64维语义向量，共6.6M参数。语义目标由训练集短语的CLIP表示经训练集PCA降维，InfoNCE温度0.07；在线不运行CLIP编码器。论文未系统消融取哪一层。

changes.title: 监督增量：整段失败前缀为正，失败后不计损失
changes.text: pre-onset把最终失败轨迹从起点到t_fail的全部步标为1，之后排除损失；成功轨迹所有步标0。它不是只把紧邻失败的2.4秒标正，也不是把失败后标负。onset对照只在前窗标正、再早标0并丢弃失败后；post-onset从前窗起一直标正；trajectory将失败全轨迹标正。其作用是改变学习信号与序列截断，未做正例数量、长度等完全匹配的控制，不能只凭此证明探针学到因果先兆。

changes.title: 联合校准：接受合格阈值，否则拒绝认证
changes.text: 分数BCE加类别加权的模式交叉熵和CLIP对齐，辅助权重均为1；Adam学习率3e-4、batch32条轨迹，最多100epoch，以验证分数损失早停patience15。阈值用LTT同时检验FPR≤α和早期TPR≥β：181个sigmoid阈值、40个起点、δ=0.1，取已接受阈值中校准早期TPR最高者，无合格阈值则abstain。作者证书针对与校准数据可交换的episode；LTT是高概率认证，max-conformal的FPR界是边际保证，两者不能只凭某次拆分是否达标就视为同一种保证或定理失效。

checks.title: 摘要86%与PPV下界都需要条件
checks.text: 摘要把漂移下误报和漏检界概括为最高86%；表7的86%实际是某目标下FPR单列、且仅统计认证子集。表内α=15%时FC的unseen FPR达标率29%，故不能将“基线最多21%”推广到所有FC行。PPV公式下界为πβ/[πβ+(1−π)α]，需真实失败率π或有效下界；论文用校准集π估计，跨技能会漂移，不能直接给部署告警一个无条件正确概率。跨任务的达标份额只有经验含义，new-task/signature三个seed复用同一unseen任务集，也不是14个独立漂移环境。

checks.title: 模式分类：合并类别、只评已告警失败，非10类全覆盖
checks.text: 表8按数据集合并最小类直到每类占失败至少5%，输出概率相加但不重训；报告合并后类别平衡准确率。自己的告警以MC α=0.2触发，取告警前2.4秒加当前步的平均模式概率；未告警episode不计入该分类评价。未见技能top-3为56.3%，多数基线39.0%、均匀随机42.9%；约44%相对提升仅对应前一个弱基线。真机top-3为70.4%对多数32.6%，但随机已60%；top-1为21.7%对20.0%。表10是逐split均值，表8是汇总后统计，不能互换或把其中100%当作整体准确率；标为oracle的行也不是所有列都高于实际告警行。

checks.title: 数据：3180是发布的仿真episode，真机另外399条
checks.text: 两底座在原LIBERO/遮挡混合各500条，GR00T在LIBERO-X为2,180条，合计3,180条仿真数据；附录明确公开的是这些仿真embedding、标签、提示及split。Kinova Gen3真机另有399条评估轨迹、254失败，底座以8任务共510条示范微调。Gemini三遍视频标注失败类型、时刻和每3秒动作短语；t_fail是模型判读的可见错误/应接管点，未报告独立人工时刻一致性。本文使用现成文字材料，本轮没有调用该标注API。

checks.title: 标注敏感性：只向后挪时刻，真机排名会翻转
checks.text: 表11不重训、不重校准，仅把每次失败标签推迟1/2秒再评分。真机VLA-Tug从25.8到26.3/26.5，SAFE-LSTM从25.1到26.8/28.9，1秒时排名已反转；LIBERO-X各拆分排名相对稳定。向后移动必然放宽“早期”，不能替代双向标注噪声检验，也没测试必须提前一个控制块才能干预。真机40个拆分是8个留出任务×5seed，new-task/signature不同seed的unseen轨迹相同，误差须按层级理解。

checks.title: 成本：0.12ms只测4090上的探针每策略调用
checks.text: 作者在一张RTX4090报告探针拟合6.8秒、权重状态26.5MB，GPU在线中位0.12ms、四CPU线程0.94ms；同步后最多2,000步测量，不是端到端尾延迟或边缘设备实测。LIBERO-X每次VLA给8动作、20Hz消费，探针每400ms才有一个新embedding；真机6动作/50Hz为120ms。0.12ms是给定embedding后的分数延迟，低延迟不意味着50Hz监测动作中途风险；拟合秒数也不含数据采集、底座微调或embedding生成。LTT每目标对约1.3ms，但仍需158–209条带标签校准episode。

checks.title: 干预证据边界：恢复是启发式案例，没有成功率对照
checks.text: 论文展示触发后暂停策略、按模式小幅移动末端或重新规划，再恢复策略。仿真包括朝放置目标移动、抓取失败时横向移动；真机以蘑菇和篮子案例说明可能的专家修正。作者明确steering启发式未系统评价；没有恢复试验总数、干预成功率或对照区间，不能把告警检测改进写成已量化的任务成功率、安全性或自动专家系统提升。

attention.headline: VLA-Tug：用失败前缀训练更早的监测信号
attention.summary: 把失败轨迹的起点至失败时刻全部标正，丢弃失败后的损失；成功轨迹全标负。用骨干embedding上的LSTM读出分数与故障模式，再以LTT同时认证误报上限和早期检测下限，无合格阈值就拒绝认证。

signals.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.

signals.title: Social Humanoid：对齐共享码本，生成互动动作
signals.paper_title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
signals.delta: 离线将ego重定向为G1并调整partner姿态保住互动几何；人/机器人独立tokenizer共享一个码本并显式对齐，再由DFoT联合生成运动、SONIC跟踪。
signals.before: 独立重定向会丢接触关系；仅把不同形态量化到同一词表，也可能各自重建良好却无法跨形态解码。
signals.after: 固定共享码本后，加入连续+离散配对对齐使H→R翻译MPJPE12.52→2.79cm、同码率0→0.78；高层直接输出G1运动，不必每次生成后再在线做优化重定向。
signals.relevance: 需要把人体互动mocap迁移到G1时，应把接触距离、partner适配和token对齐纳入数据/表示设计；用跨解码消融检验共享词表是否真正可迁移。
signals.caveat: 260小时为重定向人–人数据；姿态误差真值同样来自重定向。真机六场景每场景30次、4参与者，未做社交质量研究或主动接触力调节。部署用3张4090加4060Mobile，308ms仅低延迟配置。
signals.question: 把原始clip与双角色副本绑定划分后，对齐收益能否保留到未见伙伴与受控感知缺失下的互动响应？

evidence.label: 共享不等于对齐
evidence.context: 表A.5同一共享码本框架，无对齐vs双对齐；held-out HHI配对clip，root-relative MPJPE，参考是重定向G1。

evidence.label: 互动距离消融
evidence.context: CHI3D OmniRetarget→加接触权重→完整接触/可达保真；只加权重脚滑0.009→0.014，完整为0.0034。

evidence.label: 保留反例
evidence.context: 表1高层HHI；本方法W-MPJPE优于R2R，但检索FD和脚接触更好，不能称全部物理指标占优。

evidence.label: 部署配置
evidence.context: n=200，后一配置含133+100ms可选缓冲；相机到命令口径，非DFoT50.4ms子模块耗时或绝对最坏时延。

mechanism.title: 双遍互动重定向
mechanism.text: 先约束G1局部形状和腕肘距离，再按接触对伙伴IK/QP；伙伴保持真实人体尺度，换角色覆盖两种角色。

mechanism.title: 共享词表与配对约束
mechanism.text: 人/机器人的编码器、解码器分离，时间压缩4倍到512维并共享512-entry EMA码本；连续距离与对称离散CE共同对齐。

mechanism.title: 按agent和时间独立去噪
mechanism.text: DFoT用相对空间关系和历史生成未来motion token；不同采样日程支持反应/共同预测，30步DDIM生成后交SONIC执行。
