passages.section: S.6.4 Comparison to Real Capture Details
passages.location: S.6.4 Comparison to Real Capture Details
passages.text: To simulate the glare artifacts we measured the PSF function of the ADS6311 by disabling the transmitter and pointing an IR flashlight at the same wavelength toward the receiver. We used a small aperture and baffle to ensure light was incident on a single pixel and that there were no multipath effects being measured respectively. These 49 measured PSF’s are treated as a basis, with remaining positions interpolated by a distance-weighted sum of the 49 measured positions. We plan to add more robust lens modeling that includes a parametric form of this glare model and can be learned in a similar fashion to the IRF learning described in section S.6.3 . Error maps for each additional modeled effect (IRF, pileup, and bloom) can be found in Figure 4 . It should be noted that the discrepancy between the reported RMSE from the main paper and this figure is due to a tighter crop around the region of interest. This is in part to highlight the effects of our realistic modeling but also because the background tarp was the most challenging to match in Blender, causing error unrelated to VisionSIMs physical model but instead due to imperfections in how the ground truth depth was calculated for the tarp in Blender.

Asset curation. To help accelerate research, we release all 3 3 D assets and scripts used to create sensor-realistic datasets, lowering the need for manual asset curation, which can be a significant hurdle. Specifically, we release the 100 100 high-quality rigged scenes, some of which are shown in Fig. 5 , which have been used to create the VisionSIM dataset. These scenes have mostly been crowdsourced from sites such as BlendSwap [ 60 ] or Blender’s example scenes [ 4 ] , although some have been made or heavily modified specifically for this use case. All scenes are fully rigged, physics-baked, and validated to render without modification using the Blender version pinned to the corresponding VisionSIM release. These assets are released under the Creative Commons license (CC BY 4.0) or similar permissive licenses.

Generation pipeline. Dataset generation is driven by a single script, scripts/mkdataset.py , that wraps the same RenderConfig dataclass and render_animation backend used throughout VisionSIM’s CLI. A user specifies a directory of blend-files and an output directory; the script then (i) uniformly samples non-overlapping sub-trajectories from the animation range of each scene, or renders the whole trajectory if desired, (ii) dispatches each (scene, trajectory) pair as an asynchronous render job via BlenderClients.pool , and (iii) saves every sequence under a deterministic path which also contains the explicit configuration used to produce the sequence. All relevant metadata are stored in per-modality SQLite databases alongside the raw data. The RenderConfig dataclass exposes every relevant parameter — resolution, render device, keyframe multiplier, types of ground truth, noise threshold, and per-modality flags — entirely through the CLI, so a full reconfiguration of the dataset requires no code changes. For example, to render a 800 × 800 800\times 800 dataset at 100 100 fps with depth, normals, optical flow, and segmentation using five parallel jobs:

For the full dataset, this script was submitted to HTCondor [ 12 ] via a containerized VisionSIM image, distributing work across thousands of CPUs and hundreds of GPUs as described in Appendix S.2 . Sensor emulation (interpolation, SPC, event camera, iToF, thermal, IMU) is applied as a post-processing pass on the ground-truth renders using the same VisionSIM library functions described in Appendix S.3 , each of which has a corresponding command-line interface tool.
Suppl. Fig. 5: Example scenes from the VisionSIM dataset. A collection of diverse indoor scenes featuring different lighting conditions, materials, and ground truth annotations.

Reproducibility. Every VisionSIM release is containerized with Docker [ 57 ] and tested end-to-end in CI, ensuring that a pinned version of the library and its container can regenerate all data without any environment configuration. Users who wish to reproduce or modify the dataset only need to (i) pull the versioned Docker image corresponding to the release tag, (ii) obtain the released blend-files, and (iii) invoke mkdataset.py with the published configuration.

analysis.overview: VisionSIM将场景渲染与原始测量仿真解耦：同一高帧率参考序列可重放dToF/iToF、SPAD、事件、RGB、热和IMU，扫描真实传感器参数，得到pileup、tap间运动及热历史等结构化失效。最可用的证据是商业dToF设备的IRF拟合、实测空间PSF和逐项物理模型带来的ROI误差下降。当前证据主要是少量开环案例，尚未证明闭环控制收益；裁剪口径、相位换算、插帧质量与低层噪声模型的缺口限制直接外推。

findings.text: 世界层由Blender输出干净HDR、深度、法线、光流、分割、位姿等，并另解热传输；sensor层将其变成原始瞬态直方图、correlation taps、二值SPAD帧或事件流。与直接把理想深度加通用高斯噪声相比，改变的是观测形成过程。复用参考帧可扫描参数而无需重渲染，但传感器仿真本身仍耗算力，新的热物性/灯光历史等世界层参数也不能无成本重放。支持多模态不等于含表1所有模态，radar/audio/hyperspectral仍非现有实现。

findings.title: dToF按光子到达与探测恢复时间生成偏差
findings.text: 每像素FOV/空间权重累积反照率与距离平方衰减，映射到往返时间bin形成SRF，再卷积IRF并加入环境光到达率，从非齐次Poisson过程采样。non-paralyzable dead time内到达被丢弃，因此高通量下较早bin被优先记录，形成pileup、range walk和计数饱和；这是信号依赖偏差，非零均值白噪声。支持EWH/EDH读出与可微执行模式，但SPAD电/光串扰尚未建模，不把空间glare PSF与探测器串扰视为同一机制。

findings.title: 实机校准并非一键拟合全部参数：IRF学习，PSF独立实测
findings.text: ADS6311为256×192输出、3×3 binning（768×576 SPAD元件），约11ns dead time、754ps时间分辨率。IRF从近delta初始化，在仅背景布场景的20×20 patch真实/仿真histogram上用交叉相关+TV损失拟合1000 epochs。Glare来自关发射器后用同波长IR手电、小孔/遮光板测49个空间PSF，再距离加权插值；不是本轮证明可自动从RGB学到的光学参数。Blender镜头只近似真实畸变，retroreflector用手工高albedo替代，器件/场景校准负担要计入采用成本。

findings.title: 分项误差图支持校准收益，正文与附录裁剪不能拼成同一表
findings.text: 目视附录图4（PDF物理页36）ROI RMSE：Generic0.87m→learned IRF0.77→pileup0.74→bloom0.54。逐步加入物理效应的结果支持组合收益，但不是完整因子设计，也没有重复运行区间。正文报告总RMSE降低约1.53m，附录明确其ROI裁剪更紧，并有难匹配背景布的几何误差；因此不把正文1.53与ROI0.33m降幅视为同一对照，更不虚构全幅绝对起止值。当前只验证一个商业dToF设备和少量场景，不能直接外推所有LiDAR。

findings.title: iToF在原始tap上积分，再让失效进入深度解码
findings.text: 模型把调制/解调相关函数、反照率/距离衰减、环境DC、shot/read noise和ADC/full-well限制放在tap形成层。顺序tap通过时间错位帧积分产生撕裂/边界鬼影，频率决定c/(2f)无歧义距离。图2的基本例用20MHz三tap，单因素例分别为35MHz约4.3m范围、50ke满阱、环境光增到主动光量级、100ms运动、10e读噪声与12bit ADC。图中是受控失效展示，未证明所有真实多径/非正弦器件效应已匹配。

findings.title: 四模态实测对照是不同层级的验证，不宜汇成统一保真分数
findings.text: 图5热杯/FLIR Boson在注水后4s的平均绝对误差为真实加热动态范围7.6%，不是7.6摄氏度。Chronoptics STOP sign相位均差0.13rad；事件流由RGB迁移，对Prophesee EVK4正/负计数差1.5%/5.8%；Pi-Imaging光子探测统计模拟0.221对实测0.229。前两项为场景数字孪生端到端，后两项来自共位普通视频驱动，继承源相机响应/白平衡误差。事件总数吻合不证明逐像素时间戳、空间结构或所有运动强度均吻合，未报告大规模多设备置信区间。

findings.title: 热相机有两种历史：物体热传输与探测器热惯性
findings.text: 热源取路径追踪diffuse irradiance与吸收系数，解含传导、对流、辐射与指定温度边界的温度场；不是用当前RGB直接涂温度。对厚物体以表面+内部点云Laplacian近似体扩散，GPU稀疏隐式Euler求解；小温差辐射对固定环境温度线性化，可复用系统矩阵。随后灰体辐射为emissivity×带内黑体响应加反射LWIR，microbolometer再按a=exp(−Δt/tau)做一阶递推，产生传感器滞后和拖影，tau典型5–15ms。场景残余热与检测器拖影不可混成同一个后处理模糊核。

findings.title: 热模型覆盖热惯性，但不是完整商用红外噪声仿真
findings.text: LWIR反射采用单标量emissivity的Lambertian BRDF，未匹配材料角度/光谱特性；热输入的specular处理有近似，点云体扩散精度依赖密度和ray-parity内部测试，缺少四面体离散的收敛保证。微测辐射热计目前未模拟NETD对应时域噪声、固定图样/列条纹、平场校正间漂移、渐晕和自发射等。热杯4秒单例不能覆盖长期接触/日照历史的全部真实性，也没有独立校准环境温度。

findings.title: 事件、被动SPAD与IMU分别保留各自测量假设
findings.text: 事件模型沿用v2e：log强度随机阈值、前端低通、centre-surround与refractory丢事件；不是VisionSIM新提出的事件动力学，EVK4验证也未专门标定其带宽/恢复期。被动SPAD按1−exp(−flux×exposure)采Bernoulli，需线性化强度并用缩放因子映射绝对flux；RGB迁移受未知ISP限制。CMOS积分高帧率形成blur，再加read/shot noise、饱和、gain和量化，ISP仅基础版本、自动3A未实现。IMU从GT轨迹数值微分再加随机游走/噪声，其质量仍依赖时间采样。

findings.title: 插帧换算力：60倍来自单场景参考，不是实时控制速度
findings.text: 附录图1B在单RTX3080、目标6400fps比较RIFE/重复帧与全渲染：400fps渲染+16倍插值约20min对全渲染超过4h；后文按95分位光流约2px搜到99.8fps，称4h3min→不到4min（约60倍）。正文同一例先称native rate约200–400fps，后文又称99.8“匹配拐点”，两种质量目标/阈值未解释一致，本卡不当统一保真临界值。迭代光流倍率是假设flow随fps近似反比，并带clamp/damping；HDR未tone-map时RIFE/FILM不可靠，重投影又会留遮挡孔洞。低LPIPS与下游稀有事件/深度尾部误差并不自动等价。

findings.title: 480k是双目参考视图数，高速流主要由插值后仿真生成
findings.text: 数据100室内场景×24s×100fps×双目=480000 GT视图，1000×1000 HDR；时间点240000、总场景时长2400s是本轮按配置计算，不能当480000独立场景。SPAD16kHz来自160倍插值，事件4kHz来自40倍，普通相机25fps、IMU250Hz，另含dToF/iToF/热。空间完全对齐和时间同步是合成设定，不代表真实rig对齐鲁棒性。发布口径为GT加脚本/资产/checksum供再生，非确认所有巨量raw流已逐项下载；生成曾用HTCondor大量CPU/GPU，无本轮重建。bitpack8倍压缩是相对uint8二值存储，非任意压缩算法8倍。

findings.title: 90%是一个检测器分数，尚非传感器组合的胜率
findings.text: 图4同低光动态轨迹对比CMOS+event与SPAD+IMU，先各自重建成图像，再过零样本检测/跟踪：前者漏杯，后者报告90%confidence。它评估整条重建+检测管线，不是90%检测准确率、场景成功率或AP，也没隔离IMU和各重建器贡献。没有大规模任务集、匹配训练/成本的多seed对照；直接用raw重训可能改变排序，不能据此选定SPAD在所有低光场景更好。CARLA行人深度误差超过3m也只是迁移示例，未验证机器人碰撞或任务失败率。

findings.title: 当前是离线开环传感器平台，闭环控制和复杂介质仍未验证
findings.text: 所有当前实验围绕sensor fidelity，尚未在物理或仿真机器人闭合perception–control；100场景发布数据仅室内。中间depth/albedo等抽象不支持直接重演体散射/高阶传输，天气和波动/衍射受限，mmWave仍是未来方向。分布式render、缓存参考帧和大量插值提升离线吞吐，不等于实时可交互仿真；scene flow还需下一帧数据、按事先keyframe轨迹后处理，不能直接当任意在线相机动作下已验证的GT输出。

findings.title: 原文换算需再核查：0.13rad、40MHz不直接得到5.3cm
findings.text: 正文同时报告iToF相位均差0.13rad、40MHz及约5.3cm。按其往返相位模型，单频δd=c·δphi/(4πf)，本轮代入c=299792458m/s得约7.75cm；若采用另一有效频率、相位归一化或误差聚合，原文需补说明，不能把5.3cm当已独立核实值。热响应算例也需谨慎：按S20在60fps、tau10ms得a约0.189，从零到单位阶跃一/二/三帧约81.1/96.4/99.3%，与文中“约三帧到90%”并非精确一致。以上只是公式算术核查，不是新采集或复现，未据此推断实现一定错误。

hypotheses.title: 待验证：RGB插帧质量是否漏掉传感器输出的尾部误差？
hypotheses.text: 待验证假设：按光流设定的低RGB插帧误差，仍可能掩盖事件计数和iToF深度边界的长尾误差。仅在公开场景资产可获得时，预先选至少12条不同速度/遮挡/反光程度的短轨迹，固定几何、光照、曝光、tap时间、解码器与随机种子；以逐帧6400fps全渲染作为短片段参考，对照50/100/200/400fps渲染后RIFE、重复帧、重投影，以及1/2px光流自适应组。分别记录RGB LPIPS、事件时空匹配/正负计数误差、iToF相位MAE、边界深度p95/p99和超过阈值的坏点率，并报render+插值+sensor全耗时与峰值显存；至少3个噪声seed，按轨迹配对给区间，不把插值后的相邻帧当独立样本。阈值与轨迹分层先定，再检验“RGB已接近参考但sensor尾误差仍不收敛”的情况。若所有预设条件中LPIPS收敛同时稳定约束事件和深度尾部误差，且适应组覆盖最困难条件，则推翻该担忧在这些范围内成立的假设；若只有特定编码/曝光失败，结论限于这些机制。实验未运行，未全面检索相关工作，不能称为已证明缺陷或研究空白。

frontier_brief.title: VisionSIM：复用场景参考帧，在测量形成层重放传感器失效
frontier_brief.change_type: 仿真平台 · 传感器建模
frontier_brief.delta: 将Blender世界渲染与sensor emulation解耦，在共享深度/辐亮度/温度与时间轨迹上生成光子直方图、iToF taps、事件流等，再扫描真实器件参数。
frontier_brief.before: 只评估理想RGB/深度或叠加通用噪声，难以暴露高通量pileup、顺序tap撕裂、refractory事件丢失和历史依赖热对比。
frontier_brief.after: dToF数字孪生用拟合IRF、实测49个空间PSF与dead-time模型接近商业器件失效；热场先解传输再经灰体/探测器惯性，改变传感器配置可复用参考渲染。
frontier_brief.relevance: 研究多传感器感知失效时，可在相同场景和轨迹上区分物理测量偏差与后端模型误差；优先用目标设备原始测量校准，而非直接把理想GT视为部署输入。
frontier_brief.caveat: 现有结果为少量开环案例，未证实闭环机器人控制收益。LiDAR主文与附录ROI口径不同；0.13rad到5.3cm的换算存疑；高速流依赖插帧，HDR/遮挡有边界，热模型也未涵盖全部真实噪声。
frontier_brief.question: 按光流/LPIPS选出的渲染率，是否也能约束事件与ToF边界的尾部误差？

evidence.label: 逐项建模的ROI对照
evidence.context: 附录图4，Generic→拟合IRF→pileup→bloom，ADS6311单设备/ROI；不能与正文约1.53m全口径降幅混用。

evidence.label: 跨模态实测
evidence.value: 热动态范围MAE7.6%；正/负事件计数差1.5%/5.8%
evidence.context: 热杯注水后4秒FLIR Boson对照；事件为RGB迁移对EVK4，正/负分别统计，不代表逐事件匹配或多场景泛化。

evidence.label: 数据生成规模
evidence.context: 24s/场景、100fps、1000×1000HDR；SPAD16kHz与事件4kHz分别来自160/40倍插值，发布GT及再生资产脚本。

evidence.label: 任务证据的限度
evidence.context: 同轨迹零样本重建+检测管线与CMOS+event比较，非准确率或任务成功率，尚无闭环。

mechanism.title: 共享参考与模态前向模型
mechanism.text: 先生成GT场景数据，再物理仿真传感器；环境光与dead-time等在原始测量层改变统计，而非只污染已解码深度。

mechanism.title: 器件校准进入仿真
mechanism.text: 可微IRF拟合与独立空间PSF测量适配ADS6311；参数扫描无需重渲染已固定的世界参考，但仍有仿真与校准成本。

mechanism.title: 热场与高速采样的边界
mechanism.text: 热传输积累历史再模拟microbolometer惯性；高时间采样用render+插值，质量取决于场景速度、HDR与遮挡，并非无条件精确。

attention.reason: 可复用的传感器仿真工具，逐项建模有设备对照；少量开环案例尚不证明机器人闭环控制收益。
attention.notice: 阅读优先级判断，不是科学质量定论。

impact.comparison: 可复用的传感器仿真工具，逐项建模有设备对照；少量开环案例尚不证明机器人闭环控制收益。

passages.text: Fig. 1: A value changed at the environment–trainer boundary raises no error, the policy still learns, and only checks of the run itself notice. (a) Schematic: one value is changed on its way to the trainer; a record on each side of the boundary, compared step by step (the step ledger), disagrees at that step. (b) Pendulum, SB3’s PPO through PlugRL (E54): the mean return of each batch of 16 episodes in the trainer’s log. Blue, the median and range of the boundary-fault runs at seeds 0–2 with one value changed, the 57 of 63 that logged all 32 batches (cross: where); grey, the median and range of ten fault-free seeds; dashed, the gain threshold, 500 above the runs’ median start. (c) The 63 runs, one cell each and in the same order in every row, grouped by the field the fault changed: observations, actions, rewards, final observations, episode ends, steps. Filled: the check caught the run (step ledger: E55).

passages.section: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment–Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
passages.location: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment–Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
passages.text: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it.

passages.section: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment–Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
passages.location: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment–Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
passages.text: On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer’s log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns.

passages.section: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment–Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
passages.location: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment–Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
passages.text: Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer’s log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

An RL run has a boundary between the code that steps the environment and the trainer , which collects experience and updates the policy: the agent–environment interface [ 1 ] , drawn in software. In many stacks nobody designs it; it falls where the trainer puts it. A Gymnasium environment [ 2 ] is an object in the trainer’s process. RLlib [ 3 ] , SRL [ 4 ] and RLinf [ 5 ] run environments in workers that install the framework and join its cluster. Robot learning moves the boundary further: to simulators in other languages, machines with no GPU stack, and robots reaching a policy over the network [ 6 , 7 ] .

Many faults at this boundary are silent: they raise no error or warning [ 8 ] . Under its SAME_STEP autoreset mode, Gymnasium 1.3’s vector episode statistics drop the first reward of every episode after an environment’s first, and count its length one short, until 1.4 (Sec. IV ). Training goes on. For environments on another machine, our own evidence that the boundary was right was that the policy still learned.

We test that evidence. PlugRL makes the boundary an explicit wire protocol (Sec. II ). The environment side sends observations, applies the actions it gets back, and feeds back rewards and episode ends. A written specification and conformance checkers say what each side must do, and lockstep bridges let Stable-Baselines3 (SB3) [ 9 ] , CleanRL [ 10 ] and RLinf train through it. On one machine a run through it is deterministic, so we can compare a run with an injected fault against the same seed without it. We call a difference between what the environment took and gave and what the trainer sent and received a boundary fault . Our method is mutation testing as RLMutation [ 11 ] applies it to deep RL, and the checks that work are the ones production ML uses against training–serving skew [ 12 ] ; what we add is measuring both at the environment–trainer boundary. We find:

Neither a learning curve nor a clean evaluation shows most boundary faults (Sec. III , Fig. Abstract ). We injected stale, zeroed, swapped or rounded observations, actions and rewards, wrong episode ends and skipped steps. On Pendulum, the gain threshold we had relied on caught 1 of 21 faults at doses up to 10% of values, and 9 when every value was wrong. On a clean environment, 723 of the 728 boundary-fault runs that passed the curve checks scored like fault-free runs.

A step ledger catches and locates every boundary fault, as it must, and cheaply (Sec. III ). A boundary fault is a difference between the two sides’ records, so comparing them must catch it. We measured that it needs no fault-free run or determinism, works across machines, names the step, environment and field, and on Pendulum costs a median 3% of training time. An episode record kept at the environment catches faults in the trainer’s log.
Such faults occur in practice (Sec. IV ): in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code, and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries.
A silent fault, then, mostly changes the run rather than the policy: its weights and, for reward and log faults, the numbers it reports. The record of the experiment stops describing the experiment.

Every experiment follows a protocol written before its registered runs, most after a pilot. Changes to it go in a dated amendment. Captions, tables and appendices name each result’s experiment (E43, …), whose protocol, logs and findings are public with the code, specification and checkers: https://github.com/PlugRL .

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: Messages. A connection opens with the server’s metadata (version, chunk length H H , offered features). The client then repeats three messages (Fig. 4 ), msgpack-encoded with NumPy arrays over a WebSocket. An infer carries the observations of n n environments, their indices and their step ids; an action reply carries a chunk of H H actions; after the chunk, a feedback carries the observation it ended on, the summed reward, the termination and truncation flags, and an info map. The client resets its own environments: the feedback that ends an episode carries the terminal observation, and the next infer the reset one. A connection closes with stop (the run is over) or resync (reconnect at once).

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: What the protocol does about faults.

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: One convention, written down. The specification fixes one episode-end convention where Gymnasium has several (Sec. IV ), and states every MUST clause. A checker for each side tests against them, with active probes.

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: Structural faults are loud. The bridge rejects a message with the wrong shape, keys or environments and closes the connection. It never fills in a missing step: losing a client stops the run, and a client too many is told to stop.

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: Runs are deterministic on one machine. The bridge is a lockstep server: each trainer step sends every environment its action, and returns once every client has fed back. So two runs through it can be compared byte for byte.

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: Each side can keep its records. A wrapper at the env client can keep an episode record and half a step ledger; the bridge keeps a bridge log of the rewards it received.

passages.section: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.location: II The Boundary as a Protocol
passages.text: Adapters present an episode end as RLinf, Gymnasium ( SAME_STEP ) and SB3 expect it, so these trainers use the protocol through the environment interface they already have.

Fig. 2: Only the step ledger catches every boundary fault at every dose it ran; byte identity misses only Hopper’s 12 final observations, which training never read. The share of boundary-fault runs each check caught, seeds 0–2: 21 faults, 63 runs per dose (23 and 69 on Hopper). Pendulum and HalfCheetah E54, Hopper E56, Pusher E58; step ledger E55, E56, E58. The ledger was not run on HalfCheetah.

The faults. SB3’s PPO trained Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and Pusher, a 7-joint arm that pushes an object to a goal, through the bridge (Appendix F ), while the env client changed one field of what it sent, in one way. The observation it sent, the action it applied, the reward, or the observation an episode ended on was replaced by zeros, by the previous step’s value or by the next environment’s, or rounded through float16; an action could also be clipped to half its range. An episode end was invented, or a time limit left out or sent as a termination; on Hopper, which ends an episode when it falls, a termination was also left out or sent as a time limit. Or a step was skipped and its feedback filled in. Two log faults sat in the trainer’s own episode log, of the kind we found in Gymnasium (Sec. IV ): each episode’s first reward left out, or its length counted one short. Each fault changed one value, 1% or every value it could reach (on Pendulum also 0.1% and 10%), the same values at every seed, seeds 0–2.

The checks (Fig. 4 in the appendix). A run’s fault was caught by the gain threshold if its gain , the mean logged return at the end of training minus that at the start, fell below a bar fixed before the runs (on Pendulum, 500); by seed spread if its final return lay more than three standard deviations from the mean of ten fault-free seeds; by byte identity if its final weights differed from the fault-free run’s at the same seed; by the episode record if the trainer’s log disagreed with the env client’s record, kept before any fault, in count, length or return; and by the step ledger if the two sides’ records of any step differed.

Learning curves miss them (Fig. 2 ). At doses up to 10% of values, the gain threshold caught at most one run in ten on all four environments. With every value wrong it caught 43%, 35%, 48% and 33%, and mostly faults that broke learning or emptied the log. The seed-spread check raised few false alarms: 0, 1, 0 and 0 of ten fault-free seeds, each judged against the other nine. Yet at doses below every value it caught at most 21%. The spread of seeds explains it. One changed value moved a boundary-fault run’s final return by a median of 15, 85, 197 and 0.7; changing the seed moved it about as much or more, by standard deviations of 11, 146, 259 and 1.9.

Fig. 3: Nearly all policies behind faults that pass both curve checks score like fault-free ones. Each final policy’s clean return, the mean of 50 deterministic episodes on a fresh environment (E57, E58), in standard deviations of ten fault-free seeds. Boundary-fault runs at seeds 0–2, every dose; black, fault-free runs. Points below − 10 -10 sit on the floor, counted.

So does a clean evaluation. We ran each of the 1,060 final policies for 50 deterministic episodes on a fresh environment (Fig. 3 ). Of the runs that passed both curve checks, 5 of 255 on Pendulum and none of 473 on the other three scored more than three standard deviations below ten fault-free seeds; the other 106 runs that did had all failed a curve check. With every reward zeroed, the log reads 0, the best possible return on Pendulum and on Pusher, while the policies score − 1196 -1196 to − 1639 -1639 and − 99 -99 to − 129 -129 .

A step ledger sees every boundary fault. A wrapper around each environment, outside the env client’s code, recorded each step: the observation it had given, the action it was handed, and what it returned. A second wrapper, around the vector environment SB3 trained on, recorded what it sent and received. A boundary fault is a difference between the two, so the comparison must catch it; the test is whether it does so in practice, and at what cost. Compared step by step, the two halves caught all 189 boundary-fault runs on Pendulum, 207 on Hopper and 189 on Pusher, each at its first changed value and field, and found no difference in the 27 runs on each without one. The two added a median 3% to Pendulum’s training time ( − 5 -5 to + 9 +9 %, each run’s learn_s against the same run without them) and left all 216 runs’ weights unchanged. With the env client on a laptop and SB3 on a workstation, they caught and located all 21 faults at one value, and found no difference in the fault-free run. That run ended on other weights than on the workstation: byte identity cannot judge across machines.

The episode record sees the books. It caught every log fault, and every boundary fault that changed a reward beyond its tolerance, an episode end or some steps. It missed faults in observations, final observations and actions, ends sent as the wrong kind, and every step skipped: none changes the episodes it compares. The bridge log, kept on the trainer’s side of the wire, caught only the log faults. A record that is to catch a client’s faults has to be kept at the environment.

Byte identity sees what training reads. On one machine the weights changed in all 504 boundary-fault runs on Pendulum and HalfCheetah, and in none of 48 runs with a 1 ms delay, a float64 wire or a log fault. On Pusher, whose episodes all end at the time limit, they changed in 189 of 189. On Hopper they changed in 195 of 207, and in none of its 24 such runs. In the other 12, one final observation changed, at a fall. SB3 bootstraps from it only at a time limit, so training never read it, and the weights stayed byte-identical. The fault was real, and the step ledger caught all 12; a trainer that reads that value would have learned from it. The two faults the bridge rejects, rows out of order and a reward missing, raised within 10 s.

Why it matters when the policy learns. What these faults do, no curve check sees. They change the record: in 888 of 900 runs the final weights differ from the fault-free run’s at the same seed, and a reward or log fault changes the returns the trainer logs, as Gymnasium’s SAME_STEP statistics did (Sec. IV ). They can cost the policy: 5 of the 255 Pendulum runs that passed both curve checks, under five different faults and doses, scored more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though 13 fault-free runs cannot tell that from a rare bad seed. In one arm of a comparison, a reward or log fault would read as a difference between methods [ 13 ] . Whether a fault reaches the weights depends on how the trainer bootstraps, as Hopper’s final observations show under SB3; on harder tasks such faults can change what is learned, as time-limit handling does [ 14 ] .

The faults of Sec. III are not hypothetical (Table I ). We found some while building and checking PlugRL, many by reconciliation or a controlled comparison, and none by an error. Others were reported in multi-agent libraries, where agents that act in turn or leave early add conventions to get wrong. Every boundary fault among them is a kind we injected. Faults in a run’s lifecycle and cost, which fall outside the boundary, are in Appendix B .
TABLE I: Faults that raised no error, found in practice.

SuperSuit [ 18 ] the reset’s info overwrote the terminal observation episode end MAPPO’s SMACv2 wrapper [ 19 ] dead agents’ padded steps were trained on as real log Gymnasium 1.3 (E51) under SAME_STEP , every episode after an env’s first lost its first reward and a step (fixed in 1.4 [ 20 ] ) CleanRL [ 10 ] (E51) on Gymnasium 1.3, not the 0.29 it pins, no episode was logged RLlib 2.53 [ 21 ] a shared module logged one agent’s return, not the sum our specification (E44) for a client written from it, the server logged a return of 0

We applied the checks to the protocol itself (Table III , Appendix C ). On one machine, SB3 trained 16 Pendulum, HalfCheetah or Atari environments in its own process and behind the bridge: all nine pairs ended on byte-identical weights and logged identical episodes, and all 12 Pendulum runs behind a proxy that held every byte 0–25 ms each way ended on the in-process weights. The env client waits for each action, so latency decides when a step happens, not what it produces. The bridge added 0.4–0.6 ms a step for 16 state vectors and 2.6–3.0 ms for 16 frames. Across machines a seed no longer reproduces: two MuJoCo builds differ in the last bit at the first step. Every seed passed its gain threshold across machines, with env clients on a Windows laptop with no torch, Ray or RLinf, and on one machine, in a C++ program of under 900 lines and under RLinf, SB3 and CleanRL. Sec. III shows that threshold to be weak; the step ledger’s one fault-free run across machines, clean at every step, is the stronger evidence.

passages.section: VI The Price of the Boundary
passages.location: VI The Price of the Boundary
passages.text: On one machine an exchange costs 0.1 ms with states only and under 1 ms at 588 KiB. Between two machines it costs a latency s s plus k k copies of the observation’s P P bytes over the bandwidth B B , t = s + k ​ P / B t=s+kP/B [ 22 ] , which predicted the measured times within 3–10%. The negotiated reuse-feedback-obs feature sends each observation once instead of twice: at 588 KiB the round trip fell from 49.8 to 27.1 ms, with byte-identical weights (Appendix D ). A 184 KiB camera observation crosses our Wi-Fi path in 11.6 ms, 12% of the 100 ms we measured for one action chunk from a full-size π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} [ 23 ] in openpi [ 24 ] . A full-size π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} with LIBERO weights took one learning step through the protocol on LIBERO, which says nothing of how well RL tunes it.
Do not take a learning curve alone as evidence that the boundary is right (Sec. III ). Instead:

Keep a step ledger. Record what each environment took and gave, in a wrapper around it, and what the trainer sent and received, and compare the two step by step. Wherever we kept one (Pendulum, Hopper, Pusher), it caught and located every boundary fault we injected, on one machine and on Pendulum across two, for a median 3% of training time on Pendulum.
Count episodes at the environment. Keep the episode record next to the environment, not on the trainer’s side of the wire, and check the trainer’s log against it.

On one machine, show that a change beneath the policy leaves the weights alone , byte for byte: a change of placement, transport, latency, scheduler or protocol version (Secs. V – VI , Table II ). If it cannot, say why.

Report the boundary : where the environments ran, how they reached the trainer, the bytes per step and the time per step. State the episode-end convention, distinguish stop from resync , and never fill in a missing step.

What beneath the algorithm changes results. Implementation details change PPO’s results [ 25 , 26 ] , time limits change what is learned [ 14 ] , reporting practice changes what can be concluded [ 13 , 27 ] , and a one-bit change moves a run as far as a new seed [ 28 ] . We add the environment–trainer boundary to that list. Our faults are silent [ 8 ] , of kinds found in DRL programs [ 29 ] . Our design is mutation testing [ 30 ] as DeepCrime [ 31 ] and RLMutation [ 11 ] apply it, and RLMutation found that comparing mean rewards misses mutants because training is stochastic. The step ledger is an end-to-end check [ 32 ] that bridges what each side perceives [ 33 ] , TFX’s training–serving skew check [ 12 ] applied to the boundary.

Environments behind a channel. RL-Glue [ 34 ] made the interface language-independent. ML-Agents [ 35 ] , Godot RL Agents [ 36 ] and RLlib [ 3 ] reach environments outside the trainer; SEED RL [ 37 ] , SRL [ 4 ] and RLinf [ 5 ] keep them inside the framework. dm_env_rpc [ 38 ] has a compliance suite, the closest precedent for our checkers, but no trainer side. Gymnasium’s check_env [ 39 ] and EnvPool’s tests [ 40 ] check an environment against its API or a reference, before training; range and NaN checks would pass a stale or rounded value. openpi [ 24 ] serves policies for inference only; LeRobot’s HIL-SERL [ 7 ] runs the policy beside the robot. None of these checks a run’s record against one kept at the environment.

We chose the faults, to cover every field but info and the ways Table I shows it going wrong, and injected them into four simulated, state-based environments with dense rewards, under one trainer (SB3’s PPO) at three seeds. That the faults the curves miss leave the policy intact may not hold for sparse rewards, long horizons, replay buffers, images or real robots. The step ledger needs a wrapper around the environment, and sees nothing that goes wrong inside it; a robot reached only through its own client can be wrapped no closer than that client. We compared ledgers after each run (150 MB a run on Hopper); checking a digest of each step as the run goes is future work. The same people wrote the specification and the C++ client. We do not study environments that keep moving while the env client waits for an action, as a real robot does.
We thank Zilin Kang, who helped build PlugRL, and the reviewers for their comments.

analysis.overview: 本文将环境–训练器边界显式化为协议，并用故障注入比较“结果正常”与“运行记录正确”两种证据。多数接口错误逃过学习曲线和干净策略评测，却被放在环境外侧与训练器侧的逐步账本定位；这对分布式RL实验可信性值得优先阅读。账本的全检出来自双方记录差异这一限定定义，不是发现所有RL错误；实现为训练后对账，四个dense-reward状态环境、SB3 PPO、三个seed，未验证持续运动真机或图像故障覆盖。
analysis.notice: 完整阅读65个原文提取片段，含正文和附录A–G；固定PDF7页，目视核对物理页1/2/3/4/6/7的图1–6与表I–VI。核对故障种类/剂量、样本分母、校验盲区、计时/通信与episode计数。公开源码、注册协议和原始日志未逐项独立审计，未运行作者代码、注入故障或复现实验。本文版本中的软件问题按历史实验报告，不当作当前所有版本仍有缺陷。

findings.title: 研究增量：把“仍能学”与边界记录是否忠实分开验证
findings.text: 边界故障被定义为环境实际收到/产出的值，与trainer送出/收到的值不一致。本文将mutation testing和训练–服务偏移式对账用于该接口，并非提出新RL优化算法。错误可能只改变最终权重或日志，短任务回报仍正常；因此曲线改善和clean evaluation可验证能力，却不能替代运行数据完整性检查。“两侧差异”是可操作但有限的故障定义，不覆盖内部算法正确性。

findings.title: 协议显式约定episode结束、顺序与断连，不填造缺失step
findings.text: PlugRL以msgpack/NumPy over WebSocket交互：infer含env索引、step id与观察，action含H步chunk，feedback含末观察、累加reward、termination/truncation与info。env自己reset，结束feedback传terminal observation、下一infer传reset observation，stop与resync区分停机/重连。lockstep bridge等所有client回报再推进；shape/keys/env集合不符则拒绝，断连停止，不补造step。两侧spec checker与运行期记录互补；写了协议并不保证实现无误，作者自己也发现spec/client约定问题。

findings.title: 故障矩阵覆盖边界字段与剂量，非全面随机软件缺陷分布
findings.text: 主注入在SB3 PPO的Pendulum、HalfCheetah、Hopper、7关节Pusher上，seeds0–2。观察/动作/reward/terminal observation做zero、stale、跨env swap、float16 round，动作还半幅clip，结束标志伪造/丢失/混淆，step被跳过并补feedback；Hopper额外两种termination错误，共21或23种。另两种trainer日志错误为丢首reward与少记一步。剂量one value、1%、all，Pendulum再加0.1%与10%，同seed改同位置。未注入info内错误，也未证明该矩阵代表所有线上缺陷的概率或严重度。

findings.title: 学习曲线与干净评测大多漏检，但“不显著差”不是等价证明
findings.text: Fig1 Pendulum单值故障63次：gain/seed spread各0/63、byte63/63、episode13/63、ledger63/63；曲线仅绘57条完整记录者，6条缺日志用cross标出。图2四环境低于all剂量时gain最多检出10%、seed spread最多21%；all剂量gain也仅43/35/48/33%。gain阈值预定（Pendulum500），spread用10无故障seed的均值±3std，留一法对照误报0/1/0/0各10seed。全部1060最终策略各跑50个干净确定性episode，过两曲线检查的728次边界故障中723次不低于无故障均值3std；这不是统计等价检验，更不能称故障无害。

findings.title: 双侧账本须包住真实环境接口，而不是只比传输后日志
findings.text: 环境外wrapper在env client之前记录每step的observations、交给环境的action及返回值；另一wrapper在SB3所见vector env记录trainer送收值，按step/env/field对账。若故障恰定义为这两个观测点的差异，完整记录和正确比较应检出它，检验价值在于实现、定位与成本。单trainer端bridge log已在错误之后，只能核对自身日志，不能看见client中途篡改。部署位置因此是方法的关键，而非单纯多加一个日志文件。

findings.title: 585次账本注入全检出，不能写成四环境全部900次均验证
findings.text: E55/E56/E58账本分别检出Pendulum189、Hopper207、Pusher189次边界故障（合计585，本轮加总），均定位首个变值/字段；每环境27次无边界故障对照没有差异。图2明确HalfCheetah未跑账本，Pendulum账本也未覆盖主曲线所有剂量。跨机仅Pendulum单值21种故障全检出、一个无故障run无差异，不依赖fault-free参考训练或权重可复现。零误报是这些对照中的观察，不是任意数据/数值转换/软件栈的误报率上界。

findings.title: episode对账补日志盲区，但不能代替字段级账本
findings.text: episode record比较count、length、return，可检出本次全部两类日志错误及改变episode统计的故障；会漏观察、action、final-observation和部分结束类型错误。目视图6的step:fill（跳步补反馈）在one值与1%剂量episode各检出3/3，但all剂量为0/3；不应把正文“every step skipped”误读成所有跳步剂量都漏检。日志故障时ledger和byte identity保持正常，episode/bridge log各3/3检出。几种检查针对不同层，不宜用“ledger检测所有日志/生命周期错误”概括。

findings.title: byte identity能检验实现等价，却会漏未读字段且跨机失效
findings.text: 900边界故障中888次最终权重不同；Hopper其余12次只改fall时的final observation，SB3只在time limit才bootstrap该值，训练没读取它，故权重不变而账本有差异。日志故障/1ms延迟/float64 wire对照亦可保持权重相同。同机原进程与bridge9对、代理延迟0–25ms每向12次都保持byte-identical，但跨机MuJoCo build首step可差8.9e-16，同seed权重已不同。权重不同既不定位故障也不证明性能坏；相同权重也不能保证协议所有字段正确。

findings.title: 3%是Pendulum加账本的开销，不是bridge总价或在线报警延迟
findings.text: E55同run有/无两侧ledger的learn_s差中位+3%、范围−5到+9%，216次权重未变；负值不表示负计算成本，论文未给重复测量置信区间。这个数字仅Pendulum，不外推图像/真机。比较在每run结束后做，Hopper每run记录约150MB；在线逐step digest属未来工作，不能称已实时阻止错误。另E50原进程→bridge总时间Pendulum12.7→16.3–16.5s、HalfCheetah64.0–67.0→76.0–76.5s，增加0.37–0.58ms/16-env vector step，与3%是不同分母。

findings.title: 最小计数器例说明错误可只在报告层，修复范围需按版本说
findings.text: E51每step t给reward t，t5结束，2env×3episode应各return15、length5。Gymnasium1.3 vector统计NEXT_STEP得到6×(15,5)，SAME_STEP首两条正常后四条(14,4)；按sub-env放单环境wrapper则两mode均正常。作者报告1.4已修复，不将其当当前版本问题；CleanRL测试是把固定依赖换为1.3，并非其所pin0.29下已证实同错。自家计数器在无显式reset时也累加成(15,5)/(30,11)/(45,17)，说明计数器的reset契约须一并验证。表I其他多agent问题是引用历史报告，本轮未复查issue或补丁。

findings.title: 协议与传输资源可复用，但不构成大模型RL有效性的证据
findings.text: E46在同Wi-Fi+Tailscale路径23.7MB/s、5×1000exchange测量，588KiB观察从发两次改一次，RTT49.8→27.1ms，保持权重一致；184KiB观察11.6ms。文中拿它除以100ms的pi0.5动作块耗时，该100ms实为单GPU随机权重、5去噪步、3次启动中位，不是训练收敛或整套机器人延迟。LIBERO权重pi0.5只完成一个学习step，无性能评测。E45 env侧C++无第三方包86KB、minimal Python2包2.6MB，排除解释器；完整client222MB，不能以最小client代表所有功能，也不能将inference-only客户端与训练端当等能力比较。

findings.title: 完整性不等于算法正确或机器人安全，盲区在两个wrapper之外
findings.text: 主结论限四个状态/稠密奖励sim、单SB3 PPO、三个seed，未覆盖图像fault、稀疏长程、replay buffer或真实机器人。环境内部错误在两个记录点上可一致而漏检；只有硬件client可包裹时也无法验证它之前的物理执行/观测。lockstep环境等动作才推进，所以延迟仅改何时step；持续运动机器人不满足此条件。表II lifecycle重连与scheduler慢1.87倍的故障也不一定改变权重或边界值，需要独立生命周期/成本检查。作者称实验有事前协议、pilot后amendment和公开日志，但本轮只核论文，未独立审计原始注册/代码，不能把全部实现和外部issue标为已复现。

hypotheses.title: 待验证：在线逐step摘要能否保留定位覆盖并减少落盘成本？
hypotheses.text: 待验证假设：对每个step的规范化双侧记录计算摘要、在线比对并在差异时保留原payload，可保留离线完整账本的已测检出覆盖，同时减少正常run的落盘量。仅做本地仿真与trace回放，先写清记录字段、env/episode/step键、合法dtype/序列化转换和reset契约，固定同一环境/训练器版本；对比完整payload训练后对账、每step摘要在线对账、相同预算的抽样payload对账。复用原故障字段与one/1%/all剂量，另加预先定义的重复/乱序/断连事件和合法float64-wire阴性对照，每组至少10seed；记录检出率、首错误定位一致率、首次检测延迟、误报、训练吞吐、p95step耗时、峰值内存及落盘字节。摘要碰撞与实现bug不能被写成零概率，发现差异后需用payload确认；不执行真实机器人或跨机部署。若摘要遗漏完整记录能定位的故障、阴性对照误报，或减少落盘却使训练吞吐/尾延迟明显变差，则推翻该替代方案在所测范围内可用的假设。实验未执行，未全面检索相关工作，不能称新发现研究空白；在线摘要亦为作者已提出的未来方向。

frontier_brief.title: RL接口静默故障：双侧逐步对账，补上正常学习曲线的盲区
frontier_brief.change_type: 评测方法 · 实验完整性
frontier_brief.delta: 将环境–训练器交互写成显式协议，在真实环境接口外和trainer所见接口各记逐step账本；用故障注入与episode独立计数检验运行记录是否忠实。
frontier_brief.before: 学习曲线达到阈值、或策略在干净环境得分正常，只检查结果；形状、范围与NaN检查也可能放过stale/rounded值。
frontier_brief.after: 在已测585次账本边界故障运行中全部定位首个错误字段，另用env侧episode记录检出日志层错误；无需另外训练fault-free参考policy。
frontier_brief.relevance: 更换跨进程/网络/语言环境接入方式，或比较RL方法时，先验证边界传递与日志账本，避免把记录偏差当作算法差异。
frontier_brief.caveat: 全检出针对两侧记录差异的限定定义；HalfCheetah未测ledger，环境内部/持续运动真机未覆盖。实现为run结束后对账，3%仅Pendulum的ledger增量，非协议总开销。
frontier_brief.question: 在线每step摘要加差异payload保留，能否在相同故障覆盖下减少存储且不恶化尾延迟？

evidence.label: 曲线正常仍有故障
evidence.value: 723/728过曲线检查的故障策略未低于参考3std
evidence.context: 全部1060policy各50个干净episode；不构成统计等价或故障无害证明，参考10个无故障seed。

evidence.label: 逐step对账覆盖
evidence.context: Pendulum/Hopper/Pusher，首变值和字段定位；每环境27对照无差异，HalfCheetah未跑账本。

evidence.label: 检查互补反例
evidence.value: Hopper12次权重不变，账本仍有差异
evidence.context: 仅改fall时final observation，SB3没读取该字段；byte identity不能代替运行记录对账。日志故障则需episode计数。

evidence.label: 有限成本证据
evidence.context: +3%为同run有无ledger的learn_s差，范围−5至+9%；本文离线对账，非在线报警延迟或跨进程桥接总成本。

mechanism.title: 把约定写成协议
mechanism.text: 明确env/step索引、terminal/reset observation、termination/truncation、stop/resync；结构不合法直接拒绝，不填造step。

mechanism.title: 比较两侧实际经历
mechanism.text: 在env client外包环境记录taken/given值，与trainer接口记录按step/env/field对齐；错误后的bridge log无法独立核client。

mechanism.title: episode与逐step互补
mechanism.text: env侧独立统计count/length/return核trainer日志；字段级ledger捕获不影响episode统计的观测/动作差异。

passages.section: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration Thanks: This work has been supported by Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University Scientific Research Projects Coordination Unit under Multidisciplinary Research Project No. 3225. The source code is available at https://github.com/ozaslan/htrip .
passages.location: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration Thanks: This work has been supported by Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University Scientific Research Projects Coordination Unit under Multidisciplinary Research Project No. 3225. The source code is available at https://github.com/ozaslan/htrip .
passages.text: Frontier-based exploration systems repeatedly evaluate geodesic travel costs between robot poses and candidate viewpoints, and tour-based planners consume the full pairwise distance matrix built from them. Recomputing these matrices with one graph search per source scales with the explored map size, whereas distance caches that refresh only locally affected or newly created frontiers can retain stale costs between surviving pairs when newly discovered free space creates a global shortcut. We present H-TRIP (Hierarchical Tropical Rank-one Incremental Propagation), an exact distance index grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring for monotonically growing occupancy grids. H-TRIP partitions the known map into a spatial hierarchy with fixed boundary ports. Each unknown-to-free revelation is decomposed into efficient rank-one min-plus edge insertions at the affected leaf, and only decreased port-to-port summaries are propagated along its ancestor chain. A shared hierarchical lift evaluates the dense many-to-many matrix of shortest distances for all active query points on the occupancy map. We prove that sequential insertions preserve exact shortest-path distances on the grid. Benchmark experiments confirm exact agreement with reference searches on fully built maps and show that dense many-to-many queries at a few dozen viewpoints are up to two orders of magnitude faster than sequential k × k\times BFS. On exploration runs with sixteen robots, in-loop queries on the growing occupancy graph are 2.21 × 2.21\times – 8.59 × 8.59\times faster than co-scheduled k × k\times BFS on maps with side 256 256 , 512 512 , and 1024 1024 cells.

passages.section: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration Thanks: This work has been supported by Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University Scientific Research Projects Coordination Unit under Multidisciplinary Research Project No. 3225. The source code is available at https://github.com/ozaslan/htrip .
passages.location: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration Thanks: This work has been supported by Ankara Yildirim Beyazit University Scientific Research Projects Coordination Unit under Multidisciplinary Research Project No. 3225. The source code is available at https://github.com/ozaslan/htrip .
passages.text: Fig. 1: We tested H-TRIP in simulation, where lidar-equipped robot teams of different sizes explored occupancy grids of different side lengths. The panels show three representative frames from these runs. The yellow lattice is the leaf-tile partition, cyan markers are active frontiers, and colored polylines are assigned open tours.

Autonomous exploration is foundational in search and rescue, inspection, and reconnaissance. Mobile robot teams iteratively map free space, extract candidate frontier viewpoints, and coordinate assignments using travel cost, information gain, or both [ 1 ] . Tour-based planners repeatedly evaluate pairwise travel costs among candidate goals using geodesic distance as their spatial backbone, which can be combined with planner-specific kinematic or utility terms [ 2 , 3 , 4 ] . These geodesics are shortest paths on the free-space graph G τ = ( V τ , E τ ) G_{\tau}=(V_{\tau},E_{\tau}) of an occupancy representation or an exploration roadmap. Under undirected traversal the geodesic distance matrix is symmetric, so filling D ∈ ℝ ¯ ≥ 0 k × k D\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}^{k\times k} among k k robot poses and candidate viewpoints with the k ⁡ ( k − 1 ) / 2 k(k-1)/2 distinct pairwise distances of G τ G_{\tau} requires substantial computational effort as maps and candidate sets grow.

As sensors reveal free space, the traversable graph G τ G_{\tau} grows monotonically. Recomputing D D from scratch with one graph search per source scales with both k k and | V τ | |V_{\tau}| , and competes with the planning cycle. Newly revealed free cells can complete a doorway or corridor that shortens the true geodesic between two persisting viewpoints, making a previously cached distance stale. The challenge is to keep the geodesic distance matrix D D exact without recomputing shortest paths over the full graph after every occupancy-map update. We therefore ask how a multi-robot system can maintain exact all-pairs geodesic distances among surviving viewpoints under online monotonic map growth while keeping many-to-many queries within a planning-cycle budget.

We present H-TRIP (Hierarchical Tropical Rank-one Incremental Propagation), an exact hierarchical distance index grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring [ 5 , 6 ] that maintains pairwise geodesic distances as occupancy grows and answers many-to-many queries for assignment and tour planners on online occupancy grids. H-TRIP organizes the workspace into a balanced spatial hierarchy over fixed leaf tiles whose boundary-port sets remain fixed throughout exploration. Sensor measurements that reveal previously unknown cells as free insert local edges in G τ G_{\tau} , including newly passable cross-tile seams, and only decreased boundary-distance summaries propagate upward along the affected ancestor chain.

H-TRIP builds this hierarchy so that many-to-many geodesic distances can be evaluated by lifting each of the k k viewpoints all at once onto the boundary ports of their ancestor tiles and resolving pairwise distances as tropical products against stored boundary metrics. H-TRIP realizes its query advantage by amortizing each hierarchical lift across the entire k × k k\times k matrix. An isolated pair lookup pays that lift without sharing it, so batched many-to-many evaluation is the regime that reuses the work. Hence H-TRIP can serve as a metric backend for multi-robot assignment and tour planners that require geodesic distance.

In simulation, H-TRIP consistently preserved exact geodesic distances while reducing the cost of repeated many-to-many evaluation relative to conventional graph-search baselines. The advantage was most pronounced when multiple robot poses and frontier viewpoints were queried together, allowing hierarchical computations to be shared across the complete distance matrix.

The main contributions of this paper are: (i) an exact hierarchical distance index for monotonically growing occupancy grids based on fixed geometric interfaces and min-plus closure; (ii) a localized insertion-only maintenance procedure based on rank-one min-plus updates, with exactness established by Lemma 1 and Theorem 1; and (iii) a batched hierarchical query that recovers the complete k × k k\times k geodesic distance matrix, with exactness established by Theorem 2.

The literature most relevant to H-TRIP spans four areas: exploration planning and travel-cost maintenance, incremental replanning, hierarchical distance indexes, and dynamic shortest-path maintenance.

Exploration planners and travel-cost maintenance: Frontier exploration guides robots toward boundaries between mapped free space and unmapped terrain, balancing travel distance against information gain [ 1 ] . Tour-based planners such as FUEL [ 2 ] , TARE [ 3 ] , and RACER [ 4 ] consume pairwise travel costs over robot poses and candidate goals (frontiers), which makes geodesic path length their spatial backbone. When a new frontier cluster appears, FUEL [ 2 ] searches paths from that cluster’s candidate viewpoints and reuses cached costs for frontier clusters that did not change, so a pair of robot poses or frontier viewpoints that survive the update can retain a pre-opening length. TARE [ 3 ] localizes traveling salesperson (TSP) work through spatial partitions. As the map grows, a newly opened doorway or corridor can shorten the true geodesic between surviving viewpoints, which can cause cached surviving-pair geodesics to become stale. H-TRIP does not replace those assignment or tour layers. It supplies the geodesic distance matrix they consume and keeps that matrix exact as the map grows, so a surviving-pair shortcut is reflected without a global graph search at every update.

Incremental single-source replanning: In partially known environments, D ∗ Lite [ 7 ] and LPA ∗ [ 8 ] incrementally repair a single-source or goal-rooted search tree as edge costs change. A straightforward use of these single-source methods for k k viewpoints requires maintaining or repairing multiple search states, typically one per source. H-TRIP is not a path replanner and does not maintain a previously found tree. It maintains one hierarchical metric shared by all queried viewpoints and fills the dense k × k k\times k distance matrix by batched coordinate lifts and tropical products, leaving path construction to the tour layer that consumes those distances.

Hierarchical distance indexes: Spatial hierarchies compress distance computation by storing summaries on region boundaries. HPA ∗ [ 9 ] partitions a grid into clusters, identifies data-dependent border entrances on traversable boundaries, and caches intra-cluster entrance distances for search on an abstract graph, which returns a near-optimal path rather than an exact stored distance. HiTi [ 10 ] is closer to H-TRIP because it recursively partitions road graphs, stores precomputed minimum-cost paths among boundary nodes, and supports optimal shortest-path queries, with updates confined to ancestor path-view sets. However, in the online occupancy setting H-TRIP fixes ports geometrically before exploration, applies rank-one min-plus insertions on leaf and interface closures when cells open, propagates only decreased ancestor metrics, and evaluates the dense k × k k\times k matrix with one batched hierarchical lift shared by all viewpoints.

On road networks and static graphs, Contraction Hierarchies [ 11 ] add vertex shortcuts, whereas Customizable Route Planning (CRP) [ 12 ] and Customizable Contraction Hierarchies [ 13 ] customize metric overlays on separator cliques or nested-dissection orders. Dynamic shortest-path indexes also admit streaming maintenance under weight updates [ 14 ] . Those methods assume a known topology whose weights change. Exploration instead changes topology: newly revealed free cells insert vertices and edges that were absent from the occupancy graph. H-TRIP still keeps the tile partition and port universe geometrically fixed, independent of current passability, so an opening does not resize overlays or churn entrances.

Dense distance graphs on recursive r r -divisions support exact distances among all boundary vertices of a region inside static planar algorithms [ 15 ] . On a static preprocessed road network whose topology is already known, many-to-many tables share hierarchical search work across a source set and a target set, so filling an | S | × | T | |S|\times|T| table is cheaper than a separate query per pair [ 16 , 17 ] . H-TRIP stores tile-local port summaries and lifts only the k k active viewpoints, such that k ≪ | V τ | k\ll|V_{\tau}| , and the planner consumes a k × k k\times k geodesic distance matrix produced by one batched hierarchical lift.

Dynamic APSP and closed-semiring algebra: Demetrescu and Italiano [ 18 ] maintain fully dynamic exact all-pairs shortest paths on general directed graphs with non-negative edge weights, covering both insertions and deletions. H-TRIP applies the same rank-one decrease [ 5 , 19 , 6 ] to leaf and interface closures along the affected ancestor chain. Its exactness theorem is insertion-only occupancy growth rather than fully dynamic APSP, and its query is a batched k × k k\times k hierarchical lift rather than an O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) pair lookup.

Ramalingam and Reps [ 20 ] repair incremental shortest paths on the affected region, and Górkiewicz and Karczmarz [ 21 ] study approximate incremental APSP on sparse directed graphs. In its insertion-only occupancy-grid setting, H-TRIP remains exact by confining dense min-plus updates to the affected ancestor chain, rather than an affected-region search or an approximate APSP.

Collectively, prior work provides incremental frontier-cost caching, single-source replanning, hierarchical shortest-path representations, and general dynamic distance maintenance. H-TRIP combines (i) fixed geometric interfaces, (ii) insertion-only exact min-plus updates, and (iii) localized hierarchical propagation into one index, and evaluates the k × k k\times k geodesic distance matrix from that index, with k ≪ | V τ | k\ll|V_{\tau}| for medium-to-large maps.

passages.section: III-A Occupancy Grid and Monotonic Map Growth
passages.location: III-A Occupancy Grid and Monotonic Map Growth
passages.text: Let 𝒲 ⊂ ℝ 2 \mathcal{W}\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} be a planar workspace discretized into a uniform occupancy grid M M . Each cell is labeled unknown , free , or obstacle . Confirmed free cells induce an undirected graph G τ = ( V τ , E τ ) G_{\tau}=(V_{\tau},E_{\tau}) , where V τ V_{\tau} is the set of currently free cells and τ \tau is a discrete time index of successive occupancy graphs. By default E τ E_{\tau} joins 4 4 -adjacent free cells with unit weight, so geodesics are integers. Non-unit nonnegative cell costs, when present, become incident edge weights, and the reference search is Dijkstra’s algorithm rather than BFS. Let d G τ ​ ( u , v ) d_{G_{\tau}}(u,v) denote shortest-path length on G τ G_{\tau} , and ∞ \infty if v v is unreachable from u u . Unknown cells retain geometric slots with infinite incident weight until they are revealed free, and obstacle cells remain blocked.

passages.section: III-A Occupancy Grid and Monotonic Map Growth

passages.text: In a typical multi-robot exploration system, assignment looks up robot–frontier costs in D τ , R ​ F D_{\tau,RF} , and an open tour looks up frontier–frontier costs in D τ , F ​ F D_{\tau,FF} . Together those stages consume the D τ , R ​ F D_{\tau,RF} and D τ , F ​ F D_{\tau,FF} blocks of the geodesic matrix. The same query returns the full symmetric k × k k\times k matrix, so D τ , R ​ R D_{\tau,RR} is filled with the robot–robot geodesics. If an entry of D τ , R ​ F D_{\tau,RF} or D τ , F ​ F D_{\tau,FF} is stale, assignment or visit order can change after a doorway opens, which is why planner-facing entries of D τ D_{\tau} must remain exact on the occupancy graph after each absorbed opening .

After an opening that produces G τ + 1 G_{\tau+1} , the true geodesic between two query cells that remain in the planning list can become strictly shorter than the length that used to be correct on G τ G_{\tau} . A viewpoint persists in the cache only when its grid coordinate is unchanged. An incremental new-cluster-only cache recomputes pairwise distances only for newly appeared clusters and, for speed, leaves the remaining entries unchanged, which can leave those lengths stale after an opening [ 2 ] .

A surviving-pair shortcut occurs when two viewpoints occupy the same cells in P τ P_{\tau} and in P τ + 1 P_{\tau+1} and, after the edges Δ ​ E = E τ + 1 ∖ E τ \Delta E=E_{\tau+1}\setminus E_{\tau} of the opening, G τ + 1 G_{\tau+1} contains a path between them that is strictly shorter than the distance stored for that pair in D τ D_{\tau} .

Such a caching mechanism is the failure mode under study, because a retained entry of its matrix D ^ τ + 1 \widehat{D}_{\tau+1} can satisfy ( D ^ τ + 1 ) i ​ j = ( D τ ) i ​ j > ( D τ + 1 ) i ​ j (\widehat{D}_{\tau+1})_{ij}=(D_{\tau})_{ij}>(D_{\tau+1})_{ij} even when both cells lie far from the newly free vertices Δ ​ V \Delta V .

A distance index is a map ℐ : V τ κ → ℝ ¯ ≥ 0 κ × κ \mathcal{I}:V_{\tau}^{\kappa}\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}^{\kappa\times\kappa} whose input is an ordered list of κ \kappa cells of G τ G_{\tau} and whose output is the geodesic distance matrix on that list. Given a monotonically expanding occupancy graph G τ → G τ + 1 G_{\tau}\to G_{\tau+1} and a viewpoint list P τ + 1 ∈ V τ + 1 k P_{\tau+1}\in V_{\tau+1}^{k} , we ask for an index ℐ \mathcal{I} that meets one mathematical contract and two computational objectives: (1) exactness: after newly free cells have been absorbed, ℐ ⁡ ( P τ + 1 ) \mathcal{I}(P_{\tau+1}) equals D τ + 1 D_{\tau+1} entrywise on that graph; (2) update locality: the work that absorbs an opening is confined to the affected leaf tiles and the union of their ancestor chains; (3) many-to-many output: a single query returns D τ + 1 D_{\tau+1} .

H-TRIP applies this algebra locally: tile closures, incremental decreases, hierarchical lifts, and boundary-to-boundary composition are min-plus operations on these matrices.

The occupancy grid M M is a square n × n n\times n array of cells, partitioned recursively into square base tiles of side b ≥ 2 b\geq 2 and super-tiles of tile aggregation degree g ≥ 2 g\geq 2 whose children form a g × g g\times g block. The independent parameters are n n , b b , and g g , from which the depth and the root side follow,

and every cell of G τ G_{\tau} lies inside that root, so | V τ | ≤ b H 2 |V_{\tau}|\leq b_{H}^{2} .

For a level- ℓ \ell tile T T of side b ℓ = b ​ g ℓ b_{\ell}=bg^{\ell} , the boundary-cell set B T B_{T} is the 4 ​ b ℓ − 4 4b_{\ell}-4 perimeter cells of its geometric boundary, whether those cells are currently passable or not.
Because the boundary geometry is fixed, occupancy updates modify only stored metric values, and interface dimensions, matrix offsets, and child-to-parent index mappings remain unchanged.

Write T T for a tile of any kind, whether a base tile of side b b , a super-tile assembled from g 2 g^{2} children, or the root that spans the workspace. A parent super-tile is denoted U U and one of its children is denoted Q Q whenever both must be named together.

The matrix stored at a tile begins as an adjacency. On a base tile T T , A T A_{T} is the weighted adjacency on the vertex set V T V_{T} of all b 2 b^{2} geometric cells of T T , including currently unknown or occupied slots, so a missing or blocked step is an infinite entry and a free adjacent step is a finite weight. On a super-tile U U , every path that leaves a child does so through that child’s boundary, and A U A_{U} is the weighted adjacency of the interface graph Γ U = ( V U , E U ) \Gamma_{U}=(V_{U},E_{U}) , whose vertices V U V_{U} are those children’s boundary cells placed side by side. The Kleene star of Section IV then turns either adjacency into pairwise distances on that same vertex set,
C T = A T ∗ , S T = C T | ( B T ) × ( B T ) , C_{T}=A_{T}^{*},\qquad S_{T}=C_{T}\big|_{(B_{T})\times(B_{T})}, (7)
so A A is a local adjacency and C C is its Kleene-star closure at every level, while the vertex set of the matrix is V T V_{T} on a base tile and V U V_{U} on a super-tile.

A base tile therefore carries two cell sets (Fig. 2 ( a )). The closure C T C_{T} lives on V T V_{T} and answers tile-confined questions: each entry C T ​ ( i , j ) C_{T}(i,j) is the length of a shortest path that stays inside T T , which can exceed the planner geodesic on G τ G_{\tau} when a globally shorter route leaves T T and re-enters. The second set is the boundary B T B_{T} , the 4 ​ b − 4 4b-4 perimeter cells. The parent of T T reads only that perimeter, so the object sent upward is the summary S T S_{T} , the restriction of C T C_{T} to the Cartesian product ( B T ) × ( B T ) (B_{T})\times(B_{T}) of those perimeter indices. The stored tile matrices change with occupancy and would therefore carry the same index τ \tau as G τ G_{\tau} . We omit that subscript on C T C_{T} and S T S_{T} , keeping τ \tau on G τ G_{\tau} and D τ D_{\tau} , so the tile symbols stay uncluttered.

A super-tile U U has three cell sets (Fig. 2 ( b )). The first set is every geometric cell of the square of U U , and interior distances on that square are recovered from the two stored sets that follow. The second set is the interface vertex set
V U = ⨆ Q B Q → U , B Q → U := φ Q → U ​ ( B Q ) , V_{U}=\bigsqcup_{Q}B_{Q\to U},\qquad B_{Q\to U}:=\varphi_{Q\to U}(B_{Q}), (8)

formed by the fixed map φ Q → U \varphi_{Q\to U} that plants each child’s boundary B Q B_{Q} at a contiguous offset B Q → U B_{Q\to U} inside U U . In other words, V U V_{U} is the concatenated list of all child boundary cells used as the row and column indices of A U A_{U} and C U C_{U} , and storing the closure C U C_{U} on that list is the compression that makes the hierarchy possible. The interface Γ U = ( V U , E U ) \Gamma_{U}=(V_{U},E_{U}) puts a weighted edge between every pair in B Q → U B_{Q\to U} whose weight is the matching entry of the child’s summary, and seam edges join spatially adjacent perimeter cells of neighboring children when both cells are free. The closure on that interface is C U = A U ∗ C_{U}=A_{U}^{*} . The third set is B U ⊂ V U B_{U}\subset V_{U} , the geometric perimeter of U U . The cells where two children meet, the interior seams, stay in V U V_{U} so that C U C_{U} can route across children, and they stay out of B U B_{U} , so the summary S U S_{U} that a further parent would read lives only on the outer boundary. Thus C U C_{U} lives on V U V_{U} , and the parent-visible summary S U S_{U} lives only on B U ⊂ V U B_{U}\subset V_{U} . The geometric cells that fill the square of U U are never stored at U U , neither as an adjacency nor as a closure making the hierarchy and compression possible. The parent concatenates the four 16-cell child boundaries into the 64-index list V U V_{U} , stores C U C_{U} as a 64 × 64 64\times 64 matrix on that list, and exposes the 36-cell outer boundary B U B_{U} .

The root is a super-tile U U with an interface adjacency A U A_{U} on the children’s boundaries and a closure C U C_{U} on that interface. The root stores C U C_{U} on V U V_{U} , and a query that is not finalized lower in the tree meets there. At initialization, each base-tile closure is the Kleene star Eq. ( 5 ) of the currently known occupancy adjacency, after which parent interface graphs are formed bottom-up from child summaries and seam edges and their closures are computed recursively until the root is reached.

Each such pair is written into the decrease set Δ ​ A T \Delta A_{T} of the tile that owns it: an intra-tile edge into its base tile, a seam into the super-tile whose immediate children first separate the endpoints. At a super-tile U U , the same opening appears as decreased child summaries Δ ​ S Q \Delta S_{Q} together with newly enabled seam edges, which together form Δ ​ A U \Delta A_{U} . Whether T T is a base tile or a super-tile, a local adjacency decrease Δ ​ A T \Delta A_{T} first updates that tile’s closure C T C_{T} . Cross-child meets share projections. Every level contributes additional path candidates, and no candidate is assumed final until all relevant ancestors have been considered. Each meet therefore improves the stored entry by taking the minimum of the incumbent value and the new candidate. Pairs in different children meet at a parent for the first time, and same-child pairs are reconsidered at that parent because they may leave the child and re-enter it. At every non-root super-tile the attachments are lifted onto the parent boundary before those meets. At the root U U every still-relevant pair meets on the interface V U V_{U} .

Let G = ( V , E , ω ) G=(V,E,\omega) be undirected with nonnegative weights, and let C = A ∗ C=A^{*} be its metric closure. Inserting an undirected edge e = { u , v } e=\{u,v\} of weight w ¯ ≥ 0 \bar{w}\geq 0 , or decreasing an existing edge to w ¯ \bar{w} , produces the new closure Eq. ( 9 ) for every pair of vertices. Sequential application of the rank-one update to every inserted or decreased edge yields the metric closure of the final graph, independent of insertion order. Equivalently, after seeding all decreased edges, a min-plus pivot sweep over their endpoint set Π \Pi yields the same updated closure.

Justification. An optimal simple path either avoids the decreased edge or uses it once, in which case the old closure already contains the prefix and suffix of Eq. ( 9 ). Every new shortest path decomposes into old shortest subpaths joined at vertices in Π \Pi , so the endpoint-pivot sweep yields the same closure.
After Algorithm 1 absorbs an insertion-only opening, every stored tile closure remains exact.

Justification. Every dirty tile absorbs all decreases in its local Δ ​ A T \Delta A_{T} by Lemma 1 , so that tile’s stored closure remains exact. If the tile is not the root and the exterior summary S T S_{T} strictly decreases, those entries are written into the parent as Δ ​ A U \Delta A_{U} together with new seams, while internal entries that do not change the exterior summary stay local. This section evaluates H-TRIP on two-dimensional occupancy maps from the MovingAI benchmark [ 22 ] . The evaluation covers numerical exactness, batched query performance, incremental update cost, and multi-robot exploration, which together characterize the regime in which the hierarchy is beneficial and the cost of maintaining it as free space is revealed.

A. Setup and Exactness: The evaluation uses two settings. To assess batched query performance, every ground-truth passable cell of each map is marked observed free, so those queries include all traversable cells. The second setting places sixteen unicycle robots with onboard two-dimensional lidars, which explore occupancy grids with 5 ​ cm 5\,\mathrm{cm} cells in the frontier-based explorer of Fig. 1 . At each planning cycle the occupancy graph G τ G_{\tau} consists of the cells the fleet has explored, frontiers are extracted from that occupancy, and robot poses and frontier representatives snap onto free cells of G τ G_{\tau} . Each query is exact. Indexing uses a double buffer so that an update does not block queries. Table I names the maps used in both settings.
Table I: Evaluation maps from the MovingAI open-source set [ 22 ]

In that first setting, query points are selected homogeneously across each map. The timed k = 25 k=25 batch uses twenty-five of those points, and each reported query time is the median of ten timed repeats after three cache warm-ups. Min-plus kernels use AVX2 on an Intel Core i7-8650U, and k × k\times BFS is a scalar, single-threaded search on the same graph. Pairwise A ∗ \mathrm{A}^{*} at k = 25 k=25 is 7.3 × 7.3\times – 9.9 × 9.9\times slower than that k × k\times BFS fill on M 1 M_{1} , M 2 M_{2} , and M 3 M_{3} , and the query tables report k × k\times BFS as the sequential-search baseline. Distances in the index are uint16 with sentinel INF = 60000 \texttt{INF}=60000 , which is sufficient for the maps in this evaluation. Tables II and V time Algorithm 2 on those fully revealed maps, and Table V times the same k × k k\times k fill on the occupancy graph G τ G_{\tau} as the robots explore. Across 178,708 178{,}708 logged matrix entries compared against BFS or Dijkstra, H-TRIP produced zero mismatches.

H-TRIP is 7.28 × 7.28\times – 11.5 × 11.5\times faster than k × k\times BFS at k = 25 k=25 on M 1 M_{1} , M 2 M_{2} , M 4 M_{4} , M 5 M_{5} , and M 6 M_{6} . M 3 M_{3} is a one-cell-wide corridor maze whose query points lie thousands of cells apart, so each BFS walks a long unique path and the paired median ratio reaches 82.6 × 82.6\times . The full-build cost is amortized after twenty-four batches on M 1 M_{1} and seven on M 3 M_{3} .

On M 3 M_{3} the one-cell corridors keep each BFS on a long unique path, so the ratios stay large across the sweep (Table V ). On the street maps H-TRIP overtakes k × k\times BFS once the batch shares hierarchical lifts, and the advantage then declines at very large k k because the k × k k\times k lift has quadratic meet cost. The benefit is therefore workload dependent, because H-TRIP reuses hierarchical lifts when viewpoints are spatially distributed.

C. Incremental Update Performance: Local openings are cheap when propagation stops near the leaf, and they become expensive when decreases dirty several ancestors, which is map dependent (Table V ). A broad multi-leaf batch can exceed a BFS refill of D τ D_{\tau} , so the exploration experiment tests whether the cheap local regime occurs often enough as the fleet opens cells.

D. Multi-Robot Exploration: The runs in Table V place sixteen robots on the occupancy graph G τ G_{\tau} that the fleet has explored so far, and each paired sample fills D τ D_{\tau} at those viewpoints. A run stops earlier when free-cell coverage reaches 95 % 95\% . When coverage is still partial, k × k\times BFS searches a smaller graph than the fully revealed maps of Table II , so the exploration speedup is smaller than the full-map figure. On M 1 M_{1} coverage is nearly complete, so the ratio stays near that full-map speedup. On M 4 M_{4} a wider lidar raises coverage, so k × k\times BFS takes longer, and H-TRIP stays cheap because most of the maze is still unknown (Fig. 5 ). On M 5 M_{5} a larger leaf reduces the paired speedup, and on M 6 M_{6} occupancy is still partial while H-TRIP remains faster than k × k\times BFS. Fig. 5 plots Algorithm 1 times against cells revealed in the same step, grouped by map side, and each curve pools in-loop updates at that resolution.

This paper introduced H-TRIP, an exact hierarchical distance index for multi-robot exploration on monotonically growing occupancy grids. By combining fixed boundary ports, min-plus closure, and localized rank-one updates, H-TRIP maintains exact geodesic distances while supporting repeated many-to-many evaluation as the map expands. During multi-robot exploration, batched queries were 2.21 × 2.21\times – 8.59 × 8.59\times faster than co-scheduled k × k\times BFS while preserving exact agreement with reference searches. Update cost remains workload dependent, however, and openings that propagate through several hierarchy levels can exceed the cost of a BFS refill. The current formulation is limited to insertion-only changes in two-dimensional occupancy grids; future work will consider non-monotonic updates, lower-memory representations, and physical multi-robot validation.

analysis.overview: H-TRIP把多机器人规划的距离后端改为固定边界层次索引：地图只增添可通行格/边时，局部min-plus闭包更新向祖先传播距离下降，查询点共享边界提升，一次输出全对精确距离。可复用之处在精确增量维护与批量共享，而非新控制器或学习模型。作者在MovingAI地图与16机器人仿真中测得查询收益，但更新、全建与GB级索引不可忽略；部分开图批次的更新加查询比BFS更贵，小批查询也可明显更慢。限定为二维单调地图，不证明整任务提速或真机效果。

findings.title: 新开通道可缩短未移动端点间距离，局部缓存失效是研究动机
findings.text: 输入是二维静态场景逐步揭示的可通行图，默认无向四邻接单位边，未知格未揭示前 incident edge 为无穷；只允许unknown→free增加顶点/边，距离不增。新门洞可让两个坐标未变的机器人/前沿点之间出现远处捷径，只对新前沿刷新距离的缓存可能保留旧长距离。每轮把机器人吸附自由格及前沿medoid合为k个点，输出机器人–机器人、机器人–前沿、前沿–前沿完整对称k×k距离矩阵。它服务分配/巡游成本，不直接输出连续机器人可执行路径。

findings.title: 固定几何边界作为接口，保存局部闭包而非全图APSP
findings.text: 把n×n图分为边长b的叶块，g×g子块递归聚合。每块周界4b_l−4个格作为固定端口，不因当前是否可通行改变，矩阵维度与子父映射不变。叶子在所有b²几何格上存闭包C，对外只暴露周界限制S；父节点仅在所有子边界拼接成的接口上存闭包，并加入可通行接缝边，再暴露自身外周界。局部C只回答块内路径，可能大于离块再进入的全图路径，所以不能把叶内表当最终全局距离。此结构借用闭半环与层次距离索引思想，不是发明min-plus本身。

findings.title: 只修复下降边及受影响祖先，精确性有插入限定
findings.text: 一条无向边(a,b)降至w后，C_new(i,j)=min(C(i,j),C(i,a)+w+C(b,j),C(i,b)+w+C(a,j))。非负权最短路可选简单路径，因此新边至多用一次，前后段由旧精确闭包给出；顺序应用可处理所有降边。实现先播种所有下降边，再仅以端点集合Π做Floyd式min-plus pivot；新最短路可分解为旧最短子路加这些端点，恢复局部闭包。叶边界条目若下降才上推，父节点合并所有孩子变化后修复一次，含首次跨子块接缝。局部更新O(|Π_T|b⁴)，不是每次重跑O(b⁶)闭包；祖先O(|Π_U||V_U|²)，仍可能很贵。Lemma1与Theorem1只支持降权/插入；free→obstacle需重建叶和祖先，不在当前增量算法范围。

findings.title: 批量共享边界提升，同叶点也必须检查更高祖先
findings.text: 查询先取点到叶边界的距离行，按min-plus乘法升到父外边界；两点通过共同祖先接口的闭包连接。在最低共同祖先首次能相遇，但路径可绕出再进入，算法仍需把所有相关更高祖先候选取最小；同叶点也不能只读叶内C。Theorem2的依据是每条网格路径可压缩成接口walk、每条接口walk也能展开为可行原路径。k个点共享每层提升，层级工作写为O(k|B_Q|²+k²|B_Q|)，避免每对单独付提升成本；它仍需输出k²项，非O(1)全局点对查询或无穷可扩展索引。

findings.title: 全揭示图查询变快，但基线含实现层差异
findings.text: MovingAI六图全可通行格均已揭示，查询点均匀分布；k=25，三次warm-up后十次计时中位，i7-8650U上H-TRIP用AVX2，BFS为标量单线程。表II非单格迷宫的五图查询7.28–11.5倍快，例如M1 32.7→3.3ms、M2 554.2→49.8ms；M3单格走廊迷宫149.4→1.81ms、82.6倍，结构特殊。M1/M2/M3上每点对A*填表比k次BFS慢7.3–9.9倍，故作者以BFS作表格基线。此证据是该实现/机器上的索引对顺序搜索收益，未隔离SIMD贡献，也未比较优化并行BFS、D*Lite/LPA*多源或其他现代层次索引。

findings.title: 收益随查询点数和拓扑变化，小批可能大幅亏损
findings.text: 表III在k=2时M1/M2比值0.67/0.51，M5/M6仅0.12/0.10，即后两者查询分别约比BFS慢8.3/10倍；k=4时M5/M6仍0.70/0.66。数十点共享提升后有利，但k=256时M1/M2优势缩到1.79/2.00倍，二次meet成本增加。M3单格走廊在k=16达235倍，是长唯一通路使BFS昂贵的特殊情形，不能当一般地图结论。不同地图和b,g配置不完全相同，不能从跨图比值独立归因叶大小。

findings.title: 更新加查询可比整表BFS重算更慢
findings.text: 表IV的M1单格同叶更新0.042ms、加查询3.34ms，对BFS34.6ms有利；同叶一次16格却更新74.8ms、合计78.1ms，对BFS33.3ms更慢；64格跨叶更新242ms、合计245ms，BFS36.2ms，约慢6.8倍。M3跨叶64格合计156ms对174ms仍略优，M4同叶16格合计21.4ms对258ms显著有利，说明传播层数与地图拓扑重要，不能仅按新开格数宣称常数低成本。图5按原地图边长汇总的更新散点与bin中位也出现秒级批次；未给查询加更新加版本切换的统一deadline保证。

findings.title: 16机器人探索内查询有配对加速，未测整体探索提速
findings.text: 表V在16台unicycle、50个frontier、最多500仿真步或95%覆盖提前停止的设置中，同一步两算法对已揭示图填同一个距离矩阵；5cm栅格，LiDAR范围/扇角/射线数随run变化。M1 122→14.2ms为8.59倍，M4两设置16.7→6.08ms及23.0→6.37ms为2.75/3.61倍，M6 478→216ms为2.21倍。终态覆盖从27.1%到93.3%不等，不能把不同时刻部分图查询与全揭示地图混用；这也不是所有run都完成95%探索。表格只报查询阶段，没有与BFS控制完整探索任务的总墙钟、路径长度或到同覆盖时间对照，不能写成整任务2.21–8.59倍提速。

findings.title: 预处理与存储是采用决策的一部分
findings.text: 表II索引87–3175MB，M2全建79.9s、3175MB，要158次k=25批查询才按表中口径抵偿全建成本；M6为63.0s、1629MB、98批，M1 0.71s、87MB、24批，M3 1.07s、404MB、7批。该break-even只用全建和查询差，不包含探索中全部增量维护。结构上叶闭包b⁴项，父闭包|V_U|²项，固定边界接口压缩也仍可很大。双缓冲用于更新不阻塞查询，但表中index大小不是已证实的进程峰值内存，也未报告双缓冲拷贝/切换额外成本。

findings.title: 正确的是已吸收更新的图，不是任意动态或物理路径
findings.text: 精确性证明针对无向非负权、二维、单调揭示且更新已被索引吸收的图；动态图障碍出现/删除、代价增加、SLAM回环引起栅格重排不由现有降权机制处理。距离在自由格图上精确，不包含车体大小、动力学、避碰、通信或实际行走误差。论文仅仿真，未量化过时缓存的shortcuts发生率或造成的分配/巡游损失；证明修复所有相关距离不等于已测探索质量增益。双缓冲存在时还需确认查询图版本与规划输入一致，本轮未审计该实现。物理多机器人和非单调维护被列为未来工作。

findings.title: 数学精确性与有限数值实现的测试覆盖应分开
findings.text: 作者在178708条已记录矩阵项与BFS或Dijkstra比较中零不匹配，这支持已测图/查询/更新的实现一致性，不是穷尽所有格点组合或所有权值。实现用uint16且INF=60000，作者称足够本次地图；将系统用于更长路径、非整数成本或更大地图时需另外验证数值范围与加法，不可直接沿用无穷/任意非负实权的数学表述。十次热缓存计时重复不是多seed独立探索或尾延迟分布，论文未给这些不确定性统计；本轮也未执行代码或核原始日志。

hypotheses.title: 待验证：把更新算入后，批量索引在什么负载下仍值得使用？
hypotheses.text: 待验证假设：H-TRIP的实际优势集中在查询多、增量小且很少传播到高层的阶段，使用按负载选择的BFS查询后端能减少总规划延迟，但必须把索引维护欠账和图版本一致性计入。只在公开MovingAI地图及记录的仿真更新序列离线回放，同一图快照和同一观点列表，比较始终H-TRIP、始终优化BFS、预注册负载门槛切换；同时将BFS保持标量与可用SIMD/多线程两种配置分开报告，避免把实现资源差异归算法。对k=2/4/16/25/64/256、同叶/跨叶开图批次及b参数分层，固定CPU核/线程、内存预算和缓存预热规则；至少10条不同种子轨迹。统计全建摊销、所有更新/复制/切换/查询总墙钟、p95/p99规划可用延迟、峰值内存和逐项距离一致性；若某轮用BFS就对当前图完整重算，之后仍把延后维护成本全部记账，不能将陈旧索引输出当最新精确图。若匹配资源并计入全部成本后切换没有降低延迟，或版本切换产生任何距离错误/无界维护积压，或大部分规划周期都不达预算，则推翻该负载切换方案可用的假设。实验未执行、未创建选题，未全面查新，不宣称新研究空白；不能推广到free→obstacle等未实现维护。
